<span class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Frameless"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Apollo_11_Crew.jpg/250px-Apollo_11_Crew.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Apollo_11_Crew.jpg/500px-Apollo_11_Crew.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" alt="This official Apollo 11 crew portrait shows astronauts Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins, and Buzz Aldrin in their white NASA spacesuits, posed against softly lit backdrop of the Moon. <p id="mwag"><b id="mwaw">Apollo 11</b> (July 16–24, 1969) was the American <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaceflight" title="Spaceflight" id="mwbA">spaceflight</a> that first landed <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human" title="Human" id="mwbQ">humans</a> on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon" title="Moon" id="mwbg">Moon</a>, and the fifth <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crewed_mission" title="Crewed mission" class="mw-redirect" id="mwbw">crewed mission</a> of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA" title="NASA" id="mwcA">NASA</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program" title="Apollo program" id="mwcQ">Apollo program</a>. The mission was crewed by Commander <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armstrong" title="Neil Armstrong" id="mwcg">Neil Armstrong</a>, Command Module Pilot <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Collins_(astronaut)" title="Michael Collins (astronaut)" id="mwcw">Michael Collins</a>, and Lunar Module Pilot <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buzz_Aldrin" title="Buzz Aldrin" id="mwdA">Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin</a>, all of whom were on their second and final spaceflight.</p>

<p id="mwdQ">Launched atop a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_V" title="Saturn V" id="mwdg">Saturn V</a> rocket from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center" title="Kennedy Space Center" id="mwdw">Kennedy Space Center</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida" title="Florida" id="mweA">Florida</a> on July 16 at 13:32 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time" title="Coordinated Universal Time" id="mweQ">UTC</a>, the Apollo spacecraft consisted of three parts: the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_command_and_service_module" title="Apollo command and service module" id="mweg">command module</a> (CM), which housed the three astronauts and was the only part to return to Earth; the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_module" title="Service module" id="mwew">service module</a> (SM), which provided propulsion, electrical power, oxygen, and water to the command module; and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Module" title="Lunar Module" class="mw-redirect" id="mwfA">Lunar Module</a> (LM), which had two stages—a descent stage with a large engine and fuel tanks for landing on the Moon, and a lighter ascent stage containing a cabin for two astronauts and a small engine to return them to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_orbit" title="Lunar orbit" id="mwfQ">lunar orbit</a>. After a three-day transit, Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the surface aboard the LM <i id="mwfg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module_Eagle" title="Apollo Lunar Module Eagle" class="mw-redirect" id="mwfw">Eagle</a></i>, landing in the Sea of Tranquility (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mare_Tranquillitatis" title="Mare Tranquillitatis" id="mwgA">Mare Tranquillitatis</a>) on July 20 at 20:17 UTC while Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the CM <i id="mwgQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_module_Columbia" title="Command module Columbia" id="mwgg">Columbia</a></i>. Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon approximately six hours after landing, followed by Aldrin nineteen minutes later. Together they spent around two and a half hours walking on the surface, planting an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Flag_Assembly" title="Lunar Flag Assembly" id="mwgw">American flag</a>, speaking with President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon" title="Richard Nixon" id="mwhA">Richard Nixon</a> who was in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House" title="White House" id="mwhQ">White House</a>, deploying scientific instruments, and collecting 21.5<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwhg">&nbsp;</span>kg (47.5<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwhw">&nbsp;</span>lb) of lunar material. After more than 21 hours on the surface, they rejoined Collins in lunar orbit, and the crew returned safely to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth" title="Earth" id="mwiA">Earth</a> on July 24, splashing down in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean" title="Pacific Ocean" id="mwiQ">Pacific Ocean</a>.</p>

<p id="mwig">Apollo 11 was the culmination of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race" title="Space Race" id="mwiw">Space Race</a>, a geopolitical competition between the United States and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union" id="mwjA">Soviet Union</a> rooted in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War" id="mwjQ">Cold War</a> rivalry. It fulfilled a national goal set by President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy" title="John F. Kennedy" id="mwjg">John F. Kennedy</a> in May 1961, who had <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon" title="We choose to go to the Moon" id="mwjw">challenged</a> the United States to land a man on the Moon and return him safely before the end of the decade. The program overcame a severe setback with the fatal <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_1" title="Apollo 1" id="mwkA">Apollo 1</a> launchpad fire in January 1967 and drew on technologies developed through the preceding <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Mercury" title="Project Mercury" id="mwkQ">Mercury</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Gemini" title="Project Gemini" id="mwkg">Gemini</a> programs. The Soviet Union, despite early leads in spaceflight, was unable to match the Saturn V rocket, and its uncrewed lunar probe <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_15" title="Luna 15" id="mwkw">Luna 15</a> crashed on the Moon on July 21, while Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin were still on the lunar surface.</p>

<p id="mwlA">Armstrong's moonwalk was broadcast live to an estimated 600 million viewers, roughly one-fifth of the world's population, making it among the most-watched <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television" title="Television" id="mwlQ">television</a> events in history. Stepping onto the lunar surface, Armstrong declared: "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_small_step" title="One small step" id="mwlg">That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind</a>." <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_sample" title="Lunar sample" class="mw-redirect" id="mwlw">Lunar samples</a> returned by the mission led to the identification of three previously unrecognized minerals, and scientific instruments deployed on the surface continued returning data for years afterwards. The crew were honoured with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticker-tape_parade" title="Ticker-tape parade" id="mwmA">ticker-tape parades</a>, a world goodwill tour, and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom" title="Presidential Medal of Freedom" id="mwmQ">Presidential Medal of Freedom</a>. The command module <i id="mwmg">Columbia</i> is preserved at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum" id="mwmw">National Air and Space Museum</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C." id="mwnA">Washington, D.C.</a>, while the descent stage of <i id="mwnQ">Eagle</i> remains on the lunar surface.</p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwng" data-mw="{&quot;autoGenerated&quot;:true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwnw" aria-labelledby="Background"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Background">Background</h2></div>
<p id="mwoA">In the late 1950s and early 1960s, the United States was engaged in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War" id="mwoQ">Cold War</a>, a geopolitical rivalry with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union" id="mwog">Soviet Union</a>.<sup about="#mwt100" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976134_14-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELogsdon1976134&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976134-14&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Logsdon&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1976&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;134&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976134-14" id="mwow"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpQ">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpg">]</span></span></a></sup> On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union launched <i id="mwpw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnik_1" title="Sputnik 1" id="mwqA">Sputnik 1</a></i>, the first <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite" title="Satellite" id="mwqQ">artificial satellite</a>, surprising the world and fueling fears about Soviet technological and military capabilities. Its success demonstrated that the USSR could potentially deliver <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapon" title="Nuclear weapon" id="mwqg">nuclear weapons</a> over <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_ballistic_missile" title="Intercontinental ballistic missile" id="mwqw">intercontinental distances</a>, challenging American claims of military, economic, and technological superiority.<sup about="#mwt103" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELogsdon197613–15_15-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELogsdon197613–15&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon197613–15-15&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Logsdon&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1976&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;13–15&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon197613–15-15" id="mwrA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwrQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwrg">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwrw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwsA">This incident sparked the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnik_crisis" title="Sputnik crisis" id="mwsQ">Sputnik crisis</a> and ignited the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race" title="Space Race" id="mwsg">Space Race</a>, as both superpowers sought to demonstrate superiority in spaceflight.<sup about="#mwt106" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson19791_16-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson19791&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson19791-16&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson19791-16" id="mwsw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwtA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtQ">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwtg">]</span></span></a></sup> President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower" title="Dwight D. Eisenhower" id="mwtw">Dwight D. Eisenhower</a> responded to the challenge posed by Sputnik by creating the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA" title="NASA" id="mwuA">National Aeronautics and Space Administration</a> (NASA), and initiating <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Mercury" title="Project Mercury" id="mwuQ">Project Mercury</a>,<sup about="#mwt109" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966101–106_17-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966101–106&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966101–106-17&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Alexander&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1966&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;101–106&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966101–106-17" id="mwug"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwuw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvA">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvQ">]</span></span></a></sup> which aimed to place a man into <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geocentric_orbit" title="Geocentric orbit" id="mwvg">Earth orbit</a>.<sup about="#mwt112" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966134_18-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966134&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966134-18&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Alexander&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1966&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;134&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966134-18" id="mwvw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwwA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwwQ">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwwg">]</span></span></a></sup> The Soviets took the lead on April 12, 1961, when <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmonaut" title="Cosmonaut" class="mw-redirect" id="mwww">cosmonaut</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Gagarin" title="Yuri Gagarin" id="mwxA">Yuri Gagarin</a> became the first person in space and the first to orbit the Earth.<sup about="#mwt115" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966332–333_19-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966332–333&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966332–333-19&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Alexander&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1966&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;332–333&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander1966332–333-19" id="mwxQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwxg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxw">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwyA">]</span></span></a></sup> Nearly a month later, on May 5, 1961, Alan Shepard became the first American in space; his 15-minute flight was suborbital, not a full orbit.<sup about="#mwt118" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976121_20-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELogsdon1976121&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976121-20&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Logsdon&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1976&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;121&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976121-20" id="mwyQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwyg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwyw">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwzQ">Because the Soviet Union had <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Launch_vehicle" title="Launch vehicle" id="mwzg">launch vehicles</a> with higher lift capacity, President John F. Kennedy, Eisenhower's successor, chose a challenge that exceeded the capabilities of the existing generation of rockets, so that both countries would be starting from an equal position. A crewed mission to the Moon would serve this purpose.<sup about="#mwt121" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976112–117_21-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELogsdon1976112–117&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976112–117-21&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Logsdon&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1976&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;112–117&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon1976112–117-21" id="mwzw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw0A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0Q">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0g">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw0w">On May 25, 1961, Kennedy addressed the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress" title="United States Congress" id="mw1A">United States Congress</a> on "Urgent National Needs" and declared:</p>

<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1244412712" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" about="#mwt124" id="mw1Q" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;I believe that this nation should commit itself to achieving the goal, before this decade [1960s] is out, of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to the Earth. No single space project in this period will be more impressive to mankind, or more important for the long-range exploration of space; and none will be so difficult or expensive to accomplish. We propose to accelerate the development of the appropriate lunar space craft. We propose to develop alternate liquid and solid fuel boosters, much larger than any now being developed, until certain which is superior. We propose additional funds for other engine development and for unmanned explorations—explorations which are particularly important for one purpose which this nation will never overlook: the survival of the man who first makes this daring flight. But in a very real sense, it will not be one man going to the Moon—if we make this judgment affirmatively, it will be an entire nation. For all of us must work to put him there. &quot;},&quot;source&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Kennedy's speech to Congress&lt;ref&gt;{{cite web |url=https://www.nasa.gov/vision/space/features/jfk_speech_text.html |title=Excerpt: 'Special Message to the Congress on Urgent National Needs' |publisher=NASA |access-date=September 16, 2018 |date=May 25, 1961 |archive-date=March 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301081146/https://www.nasa.gov/vision/space/features/jfk_speech_text.html |url-status=live }}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">.mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}</style><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt124"><p>I believe that this nation should commit itself to achieving the goal, before this decade [1960s] is out, of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to the Earth. No single space project in this period will be more impressive to mankind, or more important for the long-range exploration of space; and none will be so difficult or expensive to accomplish. We propose to accelerate the development of the appropriate lunar space craft. We propose to develop alternate liquid and solid fuel boosters, much larger than any now being developed, until certain which is superior. We propose additional funds for other engine development and for unmanned explorations—explorations which are particularly important for one purpose which this nation will never overlook: the survival of the man who first makes this daring flight. But in a very real sense, it will not be one man going to the Moon—if we make this judgment affirmatively, it will be an entire nation. For all of us must work to put him there. </p></blockquote><div class="templatequotecite" about="#mwt124" id="mw1g"><p style="display: inline; padding-left: 2.3em;">—<span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>Kennedy's speech to Congress<sup about="#mwt128" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-22" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-22&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-22" id="mw1w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw2A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw2Q">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw2g">]</span></span></a></sup><span style="display:none" data-plural="0"></span></p></div>

<p id="mw2w">On September 12, 1962, Kennedy <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon" title="We choose to go to the Moon" id="mw3A">delivered another speech</a> before a crowd of about 40,000 people in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_Stadium_(Rice_University)" title="Rice Stadium (Rice University)" id="mw3Q">Rice University football stadium</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston" title="Houston" id="mw3g">Houston</a>, Texas.<sup about="#mwt133" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-23" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-23&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-23" id="mw3w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw4A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4Q">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4g">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt136" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-24" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-24&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-24" id="mw4w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw5A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5Q">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5g">]</span></span></a></sup> A widely quoted refrain from the middle portion of the speech reads as follows:</p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt137" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mw5w" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;There is no strife, no prejudice, no national conflict in outer space as yet. Its hazards are hostile to us all. Its conquest deserves the best of all mankind, and its opportunity for peaceful cooperation may never come again. But why, some say, the Moon? Why choose this as our goal? And they may well ask, why climb the highest mountain? Why, 35 years ago, [[Spirit of St. Louis|fly the Atlantic]]? Why does [[Rice–Texas football rivalry|Rice play Texas]]?\nWe choose to go to the Moon! We choose to go to the Moon&amp;nbsp;... We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard; because that goal will serve to organize and measure the best of our energies and skills, because that challenge is one that we are willing to accept, one we are unwilling to postpone, and one we intend to win, and the others, too.&lt;ref&gt;{{cite web |title=John F. Kennedy Moon Speech—Rice Stadium |publisher=NASA |access-date=March 19, 2018 |url=https://er.jsc.nasa.gov/seh/ricetalk.htm |archive-date=July 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706061817/http://er.jsc.nasa.gov/seh/ricetalk.htm |url-status=live }}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt137" id="mw6A"><p>There is no strife, no prejudice, no national conflict in outer space as yet. Its hazards are hostile to us all. Its conquest deserves the best of all mankind, and its opportunity for peaceful cooperation may never come again. But why, some say, the Moon? Why choose this as our goal? And they may well ask, why climb the highest mountain? Why, 35 years ago, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_of_St._Louis" title="Spirit of St. Louis">fly the Atlantic</a>? Why does <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice–Texas_football_rivalry" title="Rice–Texas football rivalry">Rice play Texas</a>?
We choose to go to the Moon! We choose to go to the Moon<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>... We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard; because that goal will serve to organize and measure the best of our energies and skills, because that challenge is one that we are willing to accept, one we are unwilling to postpone, and one we intend to win, and the others, too.<sup about="#mwt141" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-25" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-25&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-25" id="mw6Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw6g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6w">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7A">]</span></span></a></sup></p></blockquote>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mw7Q"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mw7g"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg/250px-John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg/500px-John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" alt="Kennedy, in a blue suit and tie, speaks at a wooden podium bearing the seal of the President of the United States. Vice President Lyndon Johnson and other dignitaries stand behind him." data-file-width="2034" data-file-height="2954" data-file-type="bitmap" height="276" width="190" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 0.75" id="mw7w"></a><figcaption id="mw8A">President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy" title="John F. Kennedy" id="mw8Q">John F. Kennedy</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon" title="We choose to go to the Moon" id="mw8g">speaking at Rice University</a> on September 12, 1962</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mw8w">In spite of that, the proposed program faced widespread opposition and was dubbed a "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boondoggle" title="Boondoggle" id="mw9A">moondoggle</a>" by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Wiener" title="Norbert Wiener" id="mw9Q">Norbert Wiener</a>, a mathematician at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology" title="Massachusetts Institute of Technology" id="mw9g">Massachusetts Institute of Technology</a>.<sup about="#mwt152" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-26&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-26" id="mw9w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw-A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-Q">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-g">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt155" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-27&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-27" id="mw-w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw_A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw_Q">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw_g">]</span></span></a></sup> The effort to land a man on the Moon already had a name: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Apollo" title="Project Apollo" class="mw-redirect" id="mw_w">Project Apollo</a>.<sup about="#mwt144" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197915_28-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197915&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197915-28&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;15&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197915-28" id="mwAQA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQI">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQM">]</span></span></a></sup> When Kennedy met with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev" title="Nikita Khrushchev" id="mwAQQ">Nikita Khrushchev</a>, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Premier of the Soviet Union" id="mwAQU">Premier of the Soviet Union</a> in June 1961, he proposed making the Moon landing a joint project, but Khrushchev declined the offer.<sup about="#mwt147" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELogsdon201132_29-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELogsdon201132&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon201132-29&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Logsdon&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2011&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;32&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELogsdon201132-29" id="mwAQY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQg">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQk">]</span></span></a></sup> Kennedy again proposed a joint expedition to the Moon in a speech to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly" title="United Nations General Assembly" id="mwAQo">United Nations General Assembly</a> on September 20, 1963.<sup about="#mwt158" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-30" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-30&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-30" id="mwAQs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQ0">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQ4">]</span></span></a></sup> The idea of a joint Moon mission was ultimately abandoned after Kennedy's death.<sup about="#mwt161" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-31" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-31&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-31" id="mwAQ8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARE">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwARM">An early and crucial decision was choosing <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_orbit_rendezvous" title="Lunar orbit rendezvous" id="mwARQ">lunar orbit rendezvous</a> over both <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_ascent" title="Direct ascent" id="mwARU">direct ascent</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_orbit_rendezvous" title="Earth orbit rendezvous" id="mwARY">Earth orbit rendezvous</a>. A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_rendezvous" title="Space rendezvous" id="mwARc">space rendezvous</a> is an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_maneuver" title="Orbital maneuver" id="mwARg">orbital maneuver</a> in which two spacecraft navigate through space and meet up. In July 1962, NASA head <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_E._Webb" title="James E. Webb" id="mwARk">James Webb</a> announced that lunar orbit rendezvous would be used<sup about="#mwt173" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-32" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-32&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-32" id="mwARo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARw">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAR0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt162" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander196685–86_33-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander196685–86&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander196685–86-33&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Alexander&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1966&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;85–86&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESwensonGrimwoodAlexander196685–86-33" id="mwAR4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAR8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASA">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASE">]</span></span></a></sup> and that the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_(spacecraft)" title="Apollo (spacecraft)" id="mwASI">Apollo spacecraft</a> would have three major parts: a command module (CM) with a cabin for the three astronauts, and the only part that returned to Earth; a service module (SM), which supported the command module with propulsion, electrical power, oxygen, and water; and a lunar module (LM) that had two stages—a descent stage for landing on the Moon, and an ascent stage to place the astronauts back into lunar orbit.<sup about="#mwt165" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197972–77_34-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197972–77&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197972–77-34&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;72–77&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197972–77-34" id="mwASM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwASQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASU">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASY">]</span></span></a></sup> This design meant the spacecraft could be launched by a single <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_V" title="Saturn V" id="mwASc">Saturn V</a> rocket that was then under development.<sup about="#mwt168" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197948–49_35-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197948–49&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197948–49-35&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;48–49&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson197948–49-35" id="mwASg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwASk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASo">[</span>35<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwASw">Technologies and techniques required for Apollo were developed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Gemini" title="Project Gemini" id="mwAS0">Project Gemini</a>.<sup about="#mwt174" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979181–182,_205–208_36-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979181–182, 205–208&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979181–182,_205–208-36&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;181–182, 205–208&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979181–182,_205–208-36" id="mwAS4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAS8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATA">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATE">]</span></span></a></sup> The Apollo project was enabled by NASA's adoption of new advances in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor_device" title="Semiconductor device" id="mwATI">semiconductor device</a>, including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal–oxide–semiconductor_field-effect_transistor" title="Metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor" class="mw-redirect" id="mwATM">metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors</a> (MOSFETs) in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interplanetary_Monitoring_Platform" title="Interplanetary Monitoring Platform" id="mwATQ">Interplanetary Monitoring Platform</a> (IMP)<sup about="#mwt179" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-37" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-37&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-37" id="mwATU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwATY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATc">[</span>37<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt182" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-38" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-38&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-38" id="mwATk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwATo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATs">[</span>38<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATw">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon" title="Silicon" id="mwAT0">silicon</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_circuit" title="Integrated circuit" id="mwAT4">integrated circuit</a> (IC) chips in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Guidance_Computer" title="Apollo Guidance Computer" id="mwAT8">Apollo Guidance Computer</a> (AGC).<sup about="#mwt185" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-39" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-39&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-39" id="mwAUA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAUE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUI">[</span>39<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAUQ">Project Apollo was abruptly halted by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_1" title="Apollo 1" id="mwAUU">Apollo 1</a> fire on January 27, 1967, in which astronauts <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Grissom" title="Gus Grissom" id="mwAUY">Gus Grissom</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_White_(astronaut)" title="Ed White (astronaut)" id="mwAUc">Ed White</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_B._Chaffee" title="Roger B. Chaffee" id="mwAUg">Roger B. Chaffee</a> died, and the subsequent investigation.<sup about="#mwt186" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979214–218_40-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979214–218&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979214–218-40&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;214–218&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979214–218-40" id="mwAUk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAUo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUs">[</span>40<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUw">]</span></span></a></sup> In October 1968, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_7" title="Apollo 7" id="mwAU0">Apollo 7</a> evaluated the command module in Earth orbit,<sup about="#mwt189" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979265–272_41-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979265–272&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979265–272-41&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;265–272&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979265–272-41" id="mwAU4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAU8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVA">[</span>41<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVE">]</span></span></a></sup> and in December <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_8" title="Apollo 8" id="mwAVI">Apollo 8</a> tested it in lunar orbit.<sup about="#mwt192" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979274–284_42-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979274–284&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979274–284-42&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;274–284&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979274–284-42" id="mwAVM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAVQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVU">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVY">]</span></span></a></sup> In March 1969, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_9" title="Apollo 9" id="mwAVc">Apollo 9</a> put the lunar module through its paces in Earth orbit,<sup about="#mwt195" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979292–300_43-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979292–300&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979292–300-43&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;292–300&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979292–300-43" id="mwAVg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAVk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVo">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVs">]</span></span></a></sup> and in May <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_10" title="Apollo 10" id="mwAVw">Apollo 10</a> conducted a "dress rehearsal" in lunar orbit. By July 1969, all was in readiness for Apollo 11 to take the final step onto the Moon.<sup about="#mwt198" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979303–312_44-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979303–312&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979303–312-44&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;303–312&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979303–312-44" id="mwAV0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAV4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAV8">[</span>44<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAWE">The Soviet Union appeared to be winning the Space Race, but its early lead was overtaken by the US <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Gemini" title="Project Gemini" id="mwAWI">Gemini program</a> and Soviet failure to develop the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N1_(rocket)" title="N1 (rocket)" id="mwAWM">N1 launcher</a>, which would have been comparable to the Saturn V.<sup about="#mwt203" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-45" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-45&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-45" id="mwAWQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAWU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWY">[</span>45<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWc">]</span></span></a></sup> Seeing these failures, the Soviets then attempted to beat the US to return lunar material to the Earth by means of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncrewed_spacecraft" title="Uncrewed spacecraft" id="mwAWg">uncrewed probes</a>. On July 13, three days before Apollo 11's launch, the Soviet Union launched <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_15" title="Luna 15" id="mwAWk">Luna 15</a>, which reached lunar orbit before Apollo 11. During descent, a malfunction caused Luna 15 to crash in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mare_Crisium" title="Mare Crisium" id="mwAWo">Mare Crisium</a> about two hours before Armstrong and Aldrin took off from the Moon's surface to return to earth. The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuffield_Radio_Astronomy_Laboratories" title="Nuffield Radio Astronomy Laboratories" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAWs">Nuffield Radio Astronomy Laboratories</a> radio telescope in England recorded transmissions from Luna 15 during its descent, and these were released in July 2009 for the 40th anniversary of Apollo 11.<sup about="#mwt206" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-46" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-46&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-46" id="mwAWw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAW0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAW4">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAW8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwAXM" aria-labelledby="Prime_crew"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Prime_crew">Prime crew</h3></div>

<table class="wikitable plainrowheaders" about="#mwt213" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwAXQ" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Spaceflight crew\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Spaceflight_crew&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;terminology&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Astronaut&quot;},&quot;position1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Commander&quot;},&quot;crew1_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Neil Armstrong]]&quot;},&quot;flights1_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Second and last&quot;},&quot;position2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Command Module Pilot&quot;},&quot;crew2_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Michael Collins (astronaut)|Michael Collins]]&quot;},&quot;flights2_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Second and last&quot;},&quot;position3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lunar Module Pilot&quot;},&quot;crew3_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Buzz Aldrin|Edwin \&quot;Buzz\&quot; Aldrin Jr.]]&quot;},&quot;flights3_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Second and last&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">

<p id="mwAXU">The initial crew assignment of Commander <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armstrong" title="Neil Armstrong" id="mwAXY">Neil Armstrong</a>, Command Module Pilot (CMP) <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Lovell" title="Jim Lovell" id="mwAXc">Jim Lovell</a>, and Lunar Module Pilot (LMP) <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buzz_Aldrin" title="Buzz Aldrin" id="mwAXg">Buzz Aldrin</a> on the backup crew for Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwAXk">&nbsp;</span>9 was officially announced on November 20, 1967.<sup about="#mwt214" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979374_47-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979374&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979374-47&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;374&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979374-47" id="mwAXo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAXs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAXw">[</span>47<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAX0">]</span></span></a></sup> Lovell and Aldrin had previously flown together as the crew of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_12" title="Gemini 12" id="mwAX4">Gemini 12</a>. Due to design and manufacturing delays in the LM, Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwAX8">&nbsp;</span>8 and Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwAYA">&nbsp;</span>9 swapped prime and backup crews, and Armstrong's crew became the backup for Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwAYE">&nbsp;</span>8. Based on the normal crew rotation scheme, Armstrong was then expected to command Apollo 11.<sup about="#mwt217" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHansen2005312–313_48-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHansen2005312–313&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005312–313-48&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hansen&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2005&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;312–313&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005312–313-48" id="mwAYI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAYM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYQ">[</span>48<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAYY">There would be one change. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Collins_(astronaut)" title="Michael Collins (astronaut)" id="mwAYc">Michael Collins</a>, the CMP on the Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwAYg">&nbsp;</span>8 crew, began experiencing trouble with his legs. Doctors diagnosed a bony growth between his fifth and sixth vertebrae, requiring surgery.<sup about="#mwt220" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001288–289_49-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001288–289&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001288–289-49&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;288–289&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001288–289-49" id="mwAYk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAYo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYs">[</span>49<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYw">]</span></span></a></sup> Lovell took his place on the Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwAY0">&nbsp;</span>8 crew, and when Collins recovered he joined Armstrong's crew as CMP. In the meantime, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Haise" title="Fred Haise" id="mwAY4">Fred Haise</a> filled in as backup LMP, and Aldrin as backup CMP for Apollo 8.<sup about="#mwt223" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECunningham2010109_50-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECunningham2010109&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECunningham2010109-50&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Cunningham&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;109&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECunningham2010109-50" id="mwAY8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZE">[</span>50<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZI">]</span></span></a></sup> Apollo 11 was the second American mission where all the crew members had prior spaceflight experience,<sup about="#mwt226" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff200090_51-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff200090&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200090-51&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;90&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200090-51" id="mwAZM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZU">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZY">]</span></span></a></sup> the first being Apollo 10.<sup about="#mwt229" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff200072_52-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff200072&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200072-52&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;72&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200072-52" id="mwAZc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZk">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZo">]</span></span></a></sup> The next was <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-26" title="STS-26" id="mwAZs">STS-26</a> in 1988.<sup about="#mwt232" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff200090_51-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff200090&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200090-51&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;90&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200090-51" id="mwAZw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZ0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZ4">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZ8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAaA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deke_Slayton" title="Deke Slayton" id="mwAaE">Deke Slayton</a> gave Armstrong the option to replace Aldrin with Lovell, since some thought Aldrin was difficult to work with. Armstrong had no issues working with Aldrin but thought it over for a day before declining. He thought Lovell deserved to command his own mission (eventually <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_13" title="Apollo 13" id="mwAaI">Apollo 13</a>).<sup about="#mwt235" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHansen2005338–339_53-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHansen2005338–339&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005338–339-53&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hansen&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2005&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;338–339&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005338–339-53" id="mwAaM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAaQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAaU">[</span>53<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAaY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAac">The Apollo 11 prime crew had none of the close cheerful camaraderie characterized by that of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_12" title="Apollo 12" id="mwAag">Apollo 12</a>. Instead, they forged an amiable working relationship. Armstrong in particular was notoriously aloof, but Collins, who considered himself a loner, confessed to rebuffing Aldrin's attempts to create a more personal relationship.<sup about="#mwt238" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001434–435_54-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001434–435&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001434–435-54&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;434–435&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001434–435-54" id="mwAak"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAao"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAas">[</span>54<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAaw">]</span></span></a></sup> Aldrin and Collins described the crew as "amiable strangers".<sup about="#mwt241" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHansen2005359_55-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHansen2005359&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005359-55&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hansen&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2005&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;359&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005359-55" id="mwAa0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAa4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAa8">[</span>55<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbA">]</span></span></a></sup> Armstrong did not agree with the assessment, and said "all the crews I was on worked very well together."<sup about="#mwt244" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHansen2005359_55-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHansen2005359&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005359-55&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hansen&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2005&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;359&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005359-55" id="mwAbE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAbI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbM">[</span>55<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwAbU" aria-labelledby="Backup_crew"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Backup_crew">Backup crew</h3></div>

<table class="wikitable plainrowheaders" about="#mwt247" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwAbY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Spaceflight crew\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Spaceflight_crew&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;terminology&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Astronaut&quot;},&quot;position1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Commander&quot;},&quot;crew1_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Jim Lovell]]&quot;},&quot;position2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Command Module Pilot&quot;},&quot;crew2_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[William Anders]]&quot;},&quot;position3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lunar Module Pilot&quot;},&quot;crew3_up&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Fred Haise]]&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">
