rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Stark_Draper_Laboratory" title="Charles Stark Draper Laboratory" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBH4">Charles Stark Draper Laboratory</a> later recalled:</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBH8"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Lunar_Module_Eagle_in_landing_configuration_in_lunar_orbit_from_the_Command_and_Service_Module_Columbia.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBIA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Lunar_Module_Eagle_in_landing_configuration_in_lunar_orbit_from_the_Command_and_Service_Module_Columbia.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Apollo_11_Lunar_Module_Eagle_in_landing_configuration_in_lunar_orbit_from_the_Command_and_Service_Module_Columbia.jpg/330px-Apollo_11_Lunar_Module_Eagle_in_landing_configuration_in_lunar_orbit_from_the_Command_and_Service_Module_Columbia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/Apollo_11_Lunar_Module_Eagle_in_landing_configuration_in_lunar_orbit_from_the_Command_and_Service_Module_Columbia.jpg/960px-Apollo_11_Lunar_Module_Eagle_in_landing_configuration_in_lunar_orbit_from_the_Command_and_Service_Module_Columbia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2480" data-file-height="2229" data-file-type="bitmap" height="279" width="310" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.25" id="mwBIE"></a><figcaption id="mwBII"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Module_Eagle" title="Lunar Module Eagle" id="mwBIM"><i id="mwBIQ">Eagle</i></a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_orbit" title="Lunar orbit" id="mwBIU">lunar orbit</a> photographed from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_module_Columbia" title="Command module Columbia" id="mwBIY"><i id="mwBIc">Columbia</i></a></figcaption></figure>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt527" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwBIg" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;To blame the computer for the Apollo 11 problems is like blaming the person who spots a fire and calls the fire department. Actually, the computer was programmed to do more than recognize error conditions. A complete set of recovery programs was incorporated into the software. The software's action, in this case, was to eliminate lower priority tasks and re-establish the more important ones. The computer, rather than almost forcing an abort, prevented an abort. If the computer hadn't recognized this problem and taken recovery action, I doubt if Apollo 11 would have been the successful Moon landing it was.&lt;ref&gt;{{cite magazine |last=Hamilton |first=Margaret H. |author-link=Margaret Hamilton (software engineer) |date=March 1, 1971 |page=13 |title=Computer Got Loaded |journal=[[Datamation]] |type=Letter |issn=0011-6963}}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt527" id="mwBIk"><p>To blame the computer for the Apollo 11 problems is like blaming the person who spots a fire and calls the fire department. Actually, the computer was programmed to do more than recognize error conditions. A complete set of recovery programs was incorporated into the software. The software's action, in this case, was to eliminate lower priority tasks and re-establish the more important ones. The computer, rather than almost forcing an abort, prevented an abort. If the computer hadn't recognized this problem and taken recovery action, I doubt if Apollo 11 would have been the successful Moon landing it was.<sup about="#mwt531" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-120" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-120&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-120" id="mwBIo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBIs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBIw">[</span>119<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBI0">]</span></span></a></sup></p></blockquote>

<p id="mwBI4">During the mission, the cause was diagnosed as the rendezvous radar switch being in the wrong position, causing the computer to process data from both the rendezvous and landing radars at the same time.<sup about="#mwt534" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969190–192_121-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team1969190–192&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969190–192-121&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;190–192&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969190–192-121" id="mwBI8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBJA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBJE">[</span>120<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBJI">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt539" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-122" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-122&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-122" id="mwBJM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBJQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBJU">[</span>121<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBJY">]</span></span></a></sup> Software engineer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Eyles" title="Don Eyles" id="mwBJc">Don Eyles</a> concluded in a 2005 Guidance and Control Conference paper that the problem was due to a hardware design bug previously seen during testing of the first uncrewed LM in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_5" title="Apollo 5" id="mwBJg">Apollo 5</a>. Having the rendezvous radar on (so it was warmed up in case of an emergency landing abort) should have been irrelevant to the computer, but an electrical phasing mismatch between two parts of the rendezvous radar system could cause the stationary antenna to appear to the computer as dithering back and forth between two positions, depending upon how the hardware randomly powered up. The extra spurious <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycle_stealing" title="Cycle stealing" id="mwBJk">cycle stealing</a>, as the rendezvous radar updated an involuntary counter, caused the computer alarms.<sup about="#mwt542" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-123" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-123&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-123" id="mwBJo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBJs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBJw">[</span>122<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBJ0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="19" id="mwBJ4" aria-labelledby="Landing"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Landing">Landing</h3></div>

<p id="mwBLI">When Armstrong again looked outside, he saw that the computer's landing system was targeting a boulder-strewn area just north and east of a <span about="#mwt543" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBLM" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;300&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;},&quot;adj&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;mid&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;-diameter&quot;},&quot;sp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;us&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">300-foot-diameter (91</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt543">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt543">m)</span> crater (later determined to be <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_(lunar_crater)" title="West (lunar crater)" id="mwBLQ">West crater</a>), so he took semi-automatic control.<sup about="#mwt544" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994196_124-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin1994196&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994196-124&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;196&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994196-124" id="mwBLU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBLY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBLc">[</span>123<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBLg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt547" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMindell2008195–197_125-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMindell2008195–197&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMindell2008195–197-125&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mindell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2008&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;195–197&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMindell2008195–197-125" id="mwBLk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBLo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBLs">[</span>124<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBLw">]</span></span></a></sup> Armstrong considered landing short of the boulder field so they could collect geological samples from it, but could not since their horizontal velocity was too high. Throughout the descent, Aldrin called out navigation data to Armstrong, who was busy piloting <i id="mwBL0">Eagle</i>.<sup about="#mwt550" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197_126-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197-126&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;197&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197-126" id="mwBL4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBL8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBMA">[</span>125<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBME">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBMI">Armstrong found a clear patch of ground and maneuvered the spacecraft towards it. As he got closer, now <span about="#mwt553" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBMM" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;250&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;},&quot;sp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;us&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">250 feet (76</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt553">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt553">m)</span> above the surface, he discovered his new landing site had a crater in it.  Now <span about="#mwt554" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBMQ" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;107&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;},&quot;sp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;us&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">107 feet (33</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt554">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt554">m)</span> above the surface, Armstrong knew their propellant supply was dwindling and was determined to land at the first possible landing site. He cleared the crater and found another patch of level ground. They were now <span about="#mwt555" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBMU" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;100&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;},&quot;sp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;us&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">100 feet (30</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt555">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt555">m)</span> from the surface, with only 90 seconds of propellant remaining. Lunar dust kicked up by the LM's engine began to impair his ability to determine the spacecraft's motion. Some large rocks jutted out of the dust cloud, and Armstrong focused on them during his descent so he could determine the spacecraft's speed.<sup about="#mwt556" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197–199_127-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197–199&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197–199-127&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;197–199&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994197–199-127" id="mwBMY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBMc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBMg">[</span>126<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBMk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBMo">A light informed Aldrin that at least one of the <span about="#mwt559" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBMs" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;67&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;in&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;cm&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;0&quot;},&quot;adj&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;on&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">67-inch (170</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt559">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt559">cm)</span> probes hanging from <i id="mwBMw">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt560" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBM0" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> footpads had touched the surface a few moments before the landing and he said: "Contact light!" Armstrong was supposed to immediately shut the engine down, as the engineers suspected the pressure caused by the engine's own exhaust reflecting off the lunar surface could make it explode, but he forgot. Three seconds later, <i id="mwBM4">Eagle</i> landed and Armstrong shut the engine down.<sup about="#mwt561" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994199_128-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin1994199&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994199-128&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;199&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994199-128" id="mwBM8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBNA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBNE">[</span>127<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBNI">]</span></span></a></sup> Aldrin immediately said "Okay, engine stop. ACA—out of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detent" title="Detent" id="mwBNM">detent</a>." Armstrong acknowledged: "Out of detent. Auto." Aldrin continued: "Mode control—both auto. Descent engine command override off. Engine arm—off. 413 is in."<sup about="#mwt564" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMindell2008226_129-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMindell2008226&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMindell2008226-129&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mindell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2008&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;226&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMindell2008226-129" id="mwBNQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBNU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBNY">[</span>128<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBNc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBNg"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Landing_Site_&amp;_West_Crater.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBNk"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Landing_Site_&amp;_West_Crater.png" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Apollo_11_Landing_Site_%26_West_Crater.png/250px-Apollo_11_Landing_Site_%26_West_Crater.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Apollo_11_Landing_Site_%26_West_Crater.png/500px-Apollo_11_Landing_Site_%26_West_Crater.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="1400" data-file-height="1400" data-file-type="bitmap" height="250" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBNo"></a><figcaption id="mwBNs">The landing site relative to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_(lunar_crater)" title="West (lunar crater)" id="mwBNw">West crater</a></figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwBN0">ACA was the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft_attitude_control" title="Spacecraft attitude control" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBN4">Attitude Control Assembly</a>—the LM's control stick. Output went to the LGC to command the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaction_control_system" title="Reaction control system" id="mwBN8">reaction control system</a> (RCS) jets to fire. "Out of Detent" meant the stick had moved away from its centered position; it was spring-centered like the turn indicator in a car. Address 413 of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Abort_Guidance_System" title="Apollo Abort Guidance System" id="mwBOA">Abort Guidance System</a> (AGS) contained the variable that indicated the LM had landed.<sup about="#mwt567" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_1_10-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 1&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_1-10" id="mwBOE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBOI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBOM">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBOQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBOU"><i id="mwBOY">Eagle</i> landed at 20:17:40 UTC on Sunday July 20 with <span about="#mwt568" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBOc" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;216&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;lb&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">216 pounds (98</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt568">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt568">kg)</span> of usable fuel remaining. Information available to the crew and mission controllers during the landing showed the LM had enough fuel for another 25 seconds of powered flight before an abort without touchdown would have become unsafe,<sup about="#mwt572" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_1_10-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 1&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_1-10" id="mwBOg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBOk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBOo">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBOs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt569" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000295_130-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000295&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000295-130&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;295&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000295-130" id="mwBOw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBO0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBO4">[</span>129<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBO8">]</span></span></a></sup> but post-mission analysis showed that the real figure was probably closer to 50 seconds.<sup about="#mwt575" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Horizons2013_131-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Horizons2013&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Horizons2013-131&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Horizons2013-131" id="mwBPA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBPE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBPI">[</span>130<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBPM">]</span></span></a></sup> Apollo 11 landed with less fuel than most subsequent missions, and the astronauts encountered a premature low fuel warning. This was later found to be the result of the propellant <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slosh_dynamics" title="Slosh dynamics" id="mwBPQ">sloshing</a> more than expected, uncovering a fuel sensor. On subsequent missions, extra <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slosh_baffle" title="Slosh baffle" id="mwBPU">anti-slosh baffles</a> were added to the tanks to prevent this.<sup about="#mwt576" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_1_10-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 1&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_1-10" id="mwBPY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBPc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBPg">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBPk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBPo">Armstrong acknowledged Aldrin's completion of the post-landing checklist with "Engine arm is off", before responding to the CAPCOM, Charles Duke, with the words, "Houston, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranquility_Base" title="Tranquility Base" id="mwBPs">Tranquility Base</a> here. The <i id="mwBPw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Module_Eagle" title="Lunar Module Eagle" id="mwBP0">Eagle</a></i> has landed." Armstrong's unrehearsed change of call sign from "Eagle" to "Tranquility Base" emphasized to listeners that landing was complete and successful.<sup about="#mwt580" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-132" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-132&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-132" id="mwBP4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBP8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBQA">[</span>131<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBQE">]</span></span></a></sup><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_lacking_reliable_references" about="#mwt577" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBQI" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Better source needed&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Better_source_needed&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;reason&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;The History Channel was a questionable source in 2003, as evidenced by the controversy surrounding [[The Men Who Killed Kennedy]].&quot;},&quot;date&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;November 2025&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_lacking_reliable_references_from_November_2025" about="#mwt577"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt577" id="mwBQM"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="The History Channel was a questionable source in 2003, as evidenced by the controversy surrounding The Men Who Killed Kennedy. (November 2025)">better<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>source<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> Duke expressed the relief at Mission Control: "Roger, Twan—Tranquility, we copy you on the ground. You got a bunch of guys about to turn blue. We're breathing again. Thanks a lot."<sup about="#mwt583" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_1_10-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ALSJ_1-10&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_1-10" id="mwBQQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBQU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBQY">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBQc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt586" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-133" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-133&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-133" id="mwBQg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBQk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBQo">[</span>132<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBQs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBQw"><span id="mwBQ0"><video poster="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv/250px--A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser" controls preload="none" data-mw-tmh="" height="141" width="250" resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogg" data-durationhint="73" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBQ4"><source src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cc/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=index&amp;utm_content=original" type="video/ogg; codecs=&quot;theora, vorbis&quot;" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720" id="mwBQ8"><source src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/cc/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv.240p.vp9.webm" type="video/webm; codecs=&quot;vp9, opus&quot;" data-width="426" data-height="240" data-transcodekey="240p.vp9.webm" id="mwBRA"><source src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/cc/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv.360p.mpeg4.mov" type="video/quicktime" data-width="640" data-height="360" data-transcodekey="360p.mpeg4.mov" id="mwBRE"><source src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/cc/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv/A_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv.480p.vp9.webm" type="video/webm; codecs=&quot;vp9, opus&quot;" data-width="854" data-height="480" data-transcodekey="480p.vp9.webm" id="mwBRI"><track kind="subtitles" type="text/vtt" src="https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php?action=timedtext&amp;title=File%3AA_New_Look_at_the_Apollo_11_Landing_Site.ogv&amp;lang=en&amp;trackformat=vtt&amp;origin=%2A" srclang="en" label="English ‪(en)‬" data-mwtitle="" data-dir="ltr" id="mwBRM"></video></span><figcaption id="mwBRQ">A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereoscopy" title="Stereoscopy" id="mwBRU">3-D</a> view from the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Reconnaissance_Orbiter" title="Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter" id="mwBRY">Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter</a> (LRO) of the Apollo 11 landing site</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBRc">Two and a half hours after landing, before preparations began for the EVA, Aldrin radioed to Earth:</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt587" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwBRg" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;This is the LM pilot. I'd like to take this opportunity to ask every person listening in, whoever and wherever they may be, to pause for a moment and contemplate the events of the past few hours and to give thanks in his or her own way.&lt;ref&gt;{{cite web |url=http://www.hq.nasa.gov/alsj/a11/a11.postland.html |title=Post-landing Activities |date=1995 |editor-last=Jones |editor-first=Eric M. |work=Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Journal |publisher=NASA |access-date=June 13, 2013 |archive-date=May 10, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130510224246/http://www.hq.nasa.gov/alsj/a11/a11.postland.html |url-status=live }}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt587" id="mwBRk"><p>This is the LM pilot. I'd like to take this opportunity to ask every person listening in, whoever and wherever they may be, to pause for a moment and contemplate the events of the past few hours and to give thanks in his or her own way.<sup about="#mwt591" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-134" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-134&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-134" id="mwBRo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBRs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBRw">[</span>133<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBR0">]</span></span></a></sup></p></blockquote>
<p id="mwBR4">He then took <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucharist" title="Eucharist" id="mwBR8">communion</a> privately. At this time NASA was still fighting a lawsuit brought by atheist <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madalyn_Murray_O'Hair" title="Madalyn Murray O'Hair" id="mwBSA">Madalyn Murray O'Hair</a> (who had objected to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_8_Genesis_reading" title="Apollo 8 Genesis reading" id="mwBSE">Apollo<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBSI">&nbsp;</span>8 crew reading from the Book of Genesis</a>) demanding that their astronauts refrain from broadcasting religious activities while in space. For this reason, Aldrin chose to refrain from directly mentioning taking communion on the Moon. Aldrin was an elder at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webster,_Texas" title="Webster, Texas" id="mwBSM">Webster</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presbyterianism" title="Presbyterianism" id="mwBSQ">Presbyterian Church</a>, and his communion kit was prepared by the pastor of the church, Dean Woodruff. Webster Presbyterian possesses the chalice used on the Moon and commemorates the event each year on the Sunday closest to July 20.<sup about="#mwt594" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994204,_623_135-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin1994204, 623&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994204,_623-135&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;204, 623&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994204,_623-135" id="mwBSU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBSY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBSc">[</span>134<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBSg">]</span></span></a></sup> The schedule for the mission called for the astronauts to follow the landing with a five-hour sleep period, but they chose to begin preparations for the EVA early, thinking they would be unable to sleep.<sup about="#mwt597" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196921–22_136-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team196921–22&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196921–22-136&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;21–22&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196921–22-136" id="mwBSk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBSo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBSs">[</span>135<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBSw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="20" id="mwBS0" aria-labelledby="Lunar_surface_operations"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Lunar_surface_operations">Lunar surface operations</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt600" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBS4" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Tranquility Base&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt601" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt600" id="mwBS8">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranquility_Base" title="Tranquility Base">Tranquility Base</a></div>

<p id="mwBTA">Preparations for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armstrong" title="Neil Armstrong" id="mwBTE">Neil Armstrong</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buzz_Aldrin" title="Buzz Aldrin" id="mwBTI">Buzz Aldrin</a> to walk on the Moon began at 23:43 UTC.<sup about="#mwt602" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107_13-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107-13&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;107&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107-13" id="mwBTM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBTQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBTU">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBTY">]</span></span></a></sup> These took longer than expected; three and a half hours instead of two.<sup about="#mwt611" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_3_137-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 3&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_3-137" id="mwBTc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBTg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBTk">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBTo">]</span></span></a></sup> During training on Earth, everything required had been neatly laid out in advance, but on the Moon the cabin contained a large number of other items as well, such as checklists, food packets, and tools.<sup about="#mwt605" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196922_138-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team196922&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196922-138&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;22&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196922-138" id="mwBTs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBTw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBT0">[</span>137<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBT4">]</span></span></a></sup> Six hours and thirty-nine minutes after landing, Armstrong and Aldrin were ready to go outside, and <i id="mwBT8">Eagle</i> was depressurized.<sup about="#mwt608" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECortright1975215_139-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECortright1975215&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECortright1975215-139&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Cortright&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1975&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;215&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECortright1975215-139" id="mwBUA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBUE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUI">[</span>138<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBUQ"><i id="mwBUU">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt612" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBUY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span></span>s hatch was opened at 02:39:33.<sup about="#mwt613" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107_13-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107-13&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;107&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000107-13" id="mwBUc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBUg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUk">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUo">]</span></span></a></sup> Armstrong initially had some difficulties squeezing through the hatch with his <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_life_support_system" title="Primary life support system" id="mwBUs">portable life support system</a> (PLSS).<sup about="#mwt622" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_3_137-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 3&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ALSJ_3-137&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_3-137" id="mwBUw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBU0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBU4">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBU8">]</span></span></a></sup> Some of the highest heart rates recorded from Apollo astronauts occurred during LM egress and ingress.<sup about="#mwt616" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975115–120_140-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975115–120&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975115–120-140&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Johnston&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Dietlein&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Berry&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1975&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;115–120&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975115–120-140" id="mwBVA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBVE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVI">[</span>139<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVM">]</span></span></a></sup> At 02:51 Armstrong began his descent to the lunar surface. The remote-control unit on his chest kept him from seeing his feet. Climbing down the nine-rung ladder, Armstrong pulled a D-ring to deploy the modular equipment stowage assembly (MESA) folded against <i id="mwBVQ">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt619" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBVU" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> side and activate the TV camera.<sup about="#mwt625" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-141" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-141&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-141" id="mwBVY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBVc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVg">[</span>140<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt628" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_4_142-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 4&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ALSJ_4-142&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_4-142" id="mwBVo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBVs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVw">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBV0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBV4">Apollo 11 used <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slow-scan_television" title="Slow-scan television" id="mwBV8">slow-scan television</a> (TV) incompatible with broadcast TV, so it was displayed on a special monitor and a conventional TV camera viewed this monitor (thus, a broadcast of a broadcast), significantly reducing the quality of the picture.<sup about="#mwt637" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Blunder_5_143-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Blunder 5&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Blunder_5-143&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Blunder_5-143" id="mwBWA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBWE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBWI">[</span>142<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBWM">]</span></span></a></sup> The signal was received at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldstone_Deep_Space_Communications_Complex" title="Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex" id="mwBWQ">Goldstone</a> in the United States, but with better fidelity by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeysuckle_Creek_Tracking_Station" title="Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station" id="mwBWU">Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station</a> near <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra" title="Canberra" id="mwBWY">Canberra</a> in Australia. Minutes later the feed was switched to the more sensitive <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkes_Observatory" title="Parkes Observatory" id="mwBWc">Parkes radio telescope</a> in Australia.<sup about="#mwt629" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287_144-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287-144&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sarkissian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;287&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287-144" id="mwBWg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBWk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBWo">[</span>143<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBWs">]</span></span></a></sup> Despite some technical and weather difficulties, black and white images of the first lunar EVA were received and broadcast to at least 600<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBWw">&nbsp;</span>million people on Earth.<sup about="#mwt632" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287_144-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287-144&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sarkissian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;287&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESarkissian2001287-144" id="mwBW0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBW4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBW8">[</span>143<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBXA">]</span></span></a></sup> Copies of this video in broadcast format were saved and are widely available, but <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_missing_tapes" title="Apollo 11 missing tapes" id="mwBXE">recordings of the original slow scan source transmission from the lunar surface</a> were likely destroyed during routine magnetic tape re-use at NASA.<sup about="#mwt638" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Blunder_5_143-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Blunder 5&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Blunder_5-143" id="mwBXI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBXM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBXQ">[</span>142<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBXU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBYk">After describing the surface dust as "very fine-grained" and "almost like a powder",<sup about="#mwt657" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_4_142-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 4&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_4-142" id="mwBYo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBYs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBYw">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBY0">]</span></span></a></sup> at 02:56:15,<sup about="#mwt660" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AT-20190723_145-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;AT-20190723&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-AT-20190723-145&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-AT-20190723-145" id="mwBY4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBY8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZA">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZE">]</span></span></a></sup> six and a half hours after landing, Armstrong stepped off <i id="mwBZI">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt643" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBZM" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> landing pad and declared: "That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind."<sup about="#mwt644" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-transcript_147-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;transcript&quot;,&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-transcript-147&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Eric Jones of the ''Apollo Lunar Surface Journal'' explains that the indefinite article \&quot;a\&quot; was intended, whether or not it was said; the intention was to contrast ''a man'' (an individual's action) and ''mankind'' (as a species).&lt;ref&gt;{{cite web|url=http://history.nasa.gov/alsj/a11/a11.step.html#1092413|title=One Small Step|last1=Jones|first1=Eric|website=Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Journal|access-date=September 6, 2019|date=April 8, 2018|archive-date=September 3, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903233224/https://history.nasa.gov/alsj/a11/a11.step.html#1092413|url-status=live}}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;},&quot;name&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;transcript&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-transcript-147" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwBZQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBZU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZY">[</span>b<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt654" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108_148-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108-148&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;108&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108-148" id="mwBZg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBZk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZo">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt663" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-149" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-149&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-149" id="mwBZw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBZ0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZ4">[</span>147<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBZ8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBaA">Armstrong intended to say "That's one small step for a man", but the word "a" is not audible in the transmission, and thus was not initially reported by most observers of the live broadcast. When later asked about his quote, Armstrong said he believed he said "for a man", and subsequent printed versions of the quote included the "a" in square brackets. One explanation for the absence may be that his accent caused him to slur the words "for a" together; another is the intermittent nature of the audio and video links to Earth, partly because of storms near Parkes Observatory. A more recent digital analysis of the tape claims to reveal the "a" may have been spoken but obscured by static. Other analysis points to the claims of static and slurring as "face-saving fabrication", and that Armstrong himself later admitted to misspeaking the line.<sup about="#mwt665" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-150" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-150&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-150" id="mwBaE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBaI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaM">[</span>148<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt668" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-151" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-151&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-151" id="mwBaU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBaY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBac">[</span>149<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBag">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt671" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-152" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-152&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-152" id="mwBak"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBao"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBas">[</span>150<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBaw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBa0">About seven minutes after stepping onto the Moon's surface, Armstrong collected a contingency soil sample using a sample bag on a stick. He then folded the bag and tucked it into a pocket on his right thigh. This was to guarantee there would be some lunar soil brought back in case an emergency required the astronauts to abandon the EVA and return to the LM.<sup about="#mwt680" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-153" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-153&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-153" id="mwBa4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBa8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbA">[</span>151<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbE">]</span></span></a></sup> Twelve minutes after the sample was collected,<sup about="#mwt672" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108_148-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108-148&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;108&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108-148" id="mwBbI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBbM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbQ">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbU">]</span></span></a></sup> he removed the TV camera from the MESA and made a panoramic sweep, then mounted it on a tripod.<sup about="#mwt681" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_3_137-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 3&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_3-137" id="mwBbY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBbc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbg">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBbk">]</span></span></a></sup> The TV camera cable remained partly coiled and presented a tripping hazard throughout the EVA. Still photography was accomplished with a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasselblad" title="Hasselblad" id="mwBbo">Hasselblad</a> camera that could be operated hand-held or mounted on Armstrong's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo/Skylab_A7L" title="Apollo/Skylab A7L" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBbs">Apollo space suit</a>.<sup about="#mwt675" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196923_154-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team196923&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196923-154&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;23&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196923-154" id="mwBbw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBb0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBb4">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBb8">]</span></span></a></sup> Aldrin joined Armstrong on the surface. He described the view with the simple phrase: "Magnificent desolation."<sup about="#mwt682" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_4_142-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 4&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_4-142" id="mwBcA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBcE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBcI">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBcM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBcQ">Armstrong said moving in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitation_of_the_Moon" title="Gravitation of the Moon" id="mwBcU">lunar gravity</a>, one-sixth of Earth's, was "even perhaps easier than the simulations<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBcY">&nbsp;</span>... It's absolutely no trouble to walk around."<sup about="#mwt687" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_4_142-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 4&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_4-142" id="mwBcc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBcg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBck">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBco">]</span></span></a></sup> Aldrin joined him on the surface and tested methods for moving around, including two-footed kangaroo hops. The PLSS backpack created a tendency to tip backward, but neither astronaut had serious problems maintaining balance. Loping became the preferred method of movement. The astronauts reported that they needed to plan their movements six or seven steps ahead. The fine soil was quite slippery. Aldrin remarked that moving from sunlight into <i id="mwBcs">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt683" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBcw" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> shadow produced no temperature change inside the suit, but the helmet was warmer in sunlight, so he felt cooler in shadow.<sup about="#mwt688" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_4_142-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 4&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_4-142" id="mwBc0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBc4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBc8">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdA">]</span></span></a></sup> The MESA failed to provide a stable work platform and was in shadow, slowing work somewhat. As they worked, the moonwalkers kicked up gray dust, which soiled the outer part of their suits.<sup about="#mwt684" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196923_154-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team196923&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196923-154&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;23&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196923-154" id="mwBdE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBdI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdM">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBdQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBdU"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Buzz_salutes_the_U.S._Flag.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBdY"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Buzz_salutes_the_U.S._Flag.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Buzz_salutes_the_U.S._Flag.jpg/250px-Buzz_salutes_the_U.S._Flag.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Buzz_salutes_the_U.S._Flag.jpg/500px-Buzz_salutes_the_U.S._Flag.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3929" data-file-height="3967" data-file-type="bitmap" height="252" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBdc"></a><figcaption id="mwBdg">Aldrin salutes the deployed United States flag on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_surface" title="Lunar surface" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBdk">lunar surface</a>.</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBdo">The astronauts planted the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Flag_Assembly" title="Lunar Flag Assembly" id="mwBds">Lunar Flag Assembly</a> containing a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_the_United_States" title="Flag of the United States" id="mwBdw">flag of the United States</a> on the lunar surface, in clear view of the TV camera. Aldrin remembered, "Of all the jobs I had to do on the Moon the one I wanted to go the smoothest was the flag raising."<sup about="#mwt692" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-theattic_155-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;theattic&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-theattic-155&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-theattic-155" id="mwBd0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBd4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBd8">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeA">]</span></span></a></sup> But the astronauts struggled with the telescoping rod and could only insert the pole about <span about="#mwt689" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBeE" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;5&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;cm&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;in&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;0&quot;},&quot;abbr&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;&quot;},&quot;order&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;flip&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">2 inches (5</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt689">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt689">cm)</span> into the hard lunar surface. Aldrin was afraid it might topple in front of TV viewers, but gave "a crisp West Point salute".<sup about="#mwt693" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-theattic_155-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;theattic&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-theattic-155" id="mwBeI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBeM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeQ">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBeY">Before Aldrin could take a photo of Armstrong with the flag, President Richard Nixon spoke to them through a telephone-radio transmission, which Nixon called "the most historic phone call ever made from the White House."<sup about="#mwt699" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-156" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-156&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-156" id="mwBec"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBeg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBek">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBeo">]</span></span></a></sup> Nixon originally had a long speech prepared to read during the phone call, but Frank Borman, who was at the White House as a NASA liaison during Apollo 11, convinced Nixon to keep his words brief.<sup about="#mwt694" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBormanSerling1988237–238_157-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBormanSerling1988237–238&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBormanSerling1988237–238-157&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Borman&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Serling&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1988&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;237–238&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBormanSerling1988237–238-157" id="mwBes"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBew"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBe0">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBe4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt700" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwBe8" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'''Nixon:''' Hello, Neil and Buzz. I'm talking to you by telephone from the Oval Room at the White House. And this certainly has to be the most historic telephone call ever made from the White House.&lt;!-- \&quot;from the White House\&quot; was not clearly audible in the transmitted audio (although perhaps the \&quot;ouse\&quot; in \&quot;House\&quot; was), but was clearly spoken in a local recording of the call and appears in the source transcript --&gt; I just can't tell you how proud we all are of what you have done. For every American, this has to be the proudest day of our lives. And for people all over the world, I am sure that&lt;!-- \&quot;that\&quot; was not clearly audible in the transmitted audio, but was clearly spoken in a local recording of the call and appears in the source transcript --&gt; they too join with Americans in recognizing what an immense feat this is. Because of what you have done, the heavens have become a part of man's world. And as you talk to us from the Sea of Tranquility, it inspires us to redouble our efforts to bring peace and tranquility to Earth. For one priceless moment in the whole history of man, all the people on this Earth are truly one: one in their pride in what you have done, and one in our prayers that you will return safely to Earth.{{pb}}\n'''Armstrong:''' Thank you, Mr. President. It's a great honor and privilege for us to be here, representing not only the United States, but men of peace of all nations, and with interest and a&lt;!-- sometimes transcribed as \&quot;the\&quot; --&gt; curiosity, and men with a vision for the future. It's an honor for us to be able to participate here today.\n'''Nixon:''' Thank you very much, and I look forward, all of us look forward, to seeing you on the Hornet on Thursday.&lt;ref&gt;{{cite web |url=https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/telephone-conversation-with-the-apollo-11-astronauts-the-moon |title=Richard Nixon: Telephone Conversation With the Apollo 11 Astronauts on the Moon |publisher=UC Santa Barbara |work=The American Presidency Project |access-date=October 26, 2018 |archive-date=March 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302083500/https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/telephone-conversation-with-the-apollo-11-astronauts-the-moon |url-status=live }}&lt;/ref&gt;&lt;ref&gt;{{cite web |title=Apollo 11 Astronauts Talk With Richard Nixon From the Surface of the Moon – AT&amp;T Archives |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ieGKIh3koAI |publisher=AT&amp;T Tech Channel |date=July 20, 2012 |via=YouTube |access-date=December 5, 2020 |archive-date=May 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522063525/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ieGKIh3koAI |url-status=live }}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt700" id="mwBfA"><p><b>Nixon:</b> Hello, Neil and Buzz. I'm talking to you by telephone from the Oval Room at the White House. And this certainly has to be the most historic telephone call ever made from the White House. I just can't tell you how proud we all are of what you have done. For every American, this has to be the proudest day of our lives. And for people all over the world, I am sure that they too join with Americans in recognizing what an immense feat this is. Because of what you have done, the heavens have become a part of man's world. And as you talk to us from the Sea of Tranquility, it inspires us to redouble our efforts to bring peace and tranquility to Earth. For one priceless moment in the whole history of man, all the people on this Earth are truly one: one in their pride in what you have done, and one in our prayers that you will return safely to Earth.</p><div class="paragraphbreak" style="margin-top:0.5em"></div>
<p><b>Armstrong:</b> Thank you, Mr. President. It's a great honor and privilege for us to be here, representing not only the United States, but men of peace of all nations, and with interest and a curiosity, and men with a vision for the future. It's an honor for us to be able to participate here today.</p>
<p><b>Nixon:</b> Thank you very much, and I look forward, all of us look forward, to seeing you on the Hornet on Thursday.<sup about="#mwt704" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-158" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-158&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-158" id="mwBfE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBfI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfM">[</span>156<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt709" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-159" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-159&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-159" id="mwBfU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBfY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfc">[</span>157<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBfg">]</span></span></a></sup></p></blockquote>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBfk"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Buzz_Aldrin's_bootprint_on_the_Moon,_AS11-40-5877.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBfo"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Buzz_Aldrin's_bootprint_on_the_Moon,_AS11-40-5877.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Buzz_Aldrin%27s_bootprint_on_the_Moon%2C_AS11-40-5877.jpg/250px-Buzz_Aldrin%27s_bootprint_on_the_Moon%2C_AS11-40-5877.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Buzz_Aldrin%27s_bootprint_on_the_Moon%2C_AS11-40-5877.jpg/500px-Buzz_Aldrin%27s_bootprint_on_the_Moon%2C_AS11-40-5877.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="10556" data-file-height="10569" data-file-type="bitmap" height="250" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBfs"></a><figcaption id="mwBfw">Aldrin's bootprint, part of an experiment to test the properties of the lunar <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regolith" title="Regolith" id="mwBf0">regolith</a></figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBf4">They deployed the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Apollo_Scientific_Experiments_Package" title="Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBf8">EASEP</a>, which included a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passive_Seismic_Experiment_Package" title="Passive Seismic Experiment Package" id="mwBgA">Passive Seismic Experiment Package</a> used to measure <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonquake" title="Moonquake" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBgE">moonquakes</a> and a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_Ranging_Retroflector" title="Laser Ranging Retroflector" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBgI">retroreflector</a> array used for the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_laser_ranging_experiment" title="Lunar laser ranging experiment" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBgM">lunar laser ranging experiment</a>.<sup about="#mwt717" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-EASEP_Deployment_and_Closeout_160-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;EASEP Deployment and Closeout&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-EASEP_Deployment_and_Closeout-160" id="mwBgQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBgU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBgY">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBgc">]</span></span></a></sup> Then Armstrong walked <span about="#mwt712" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBgg" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;196&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">196 feet (60</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt712">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt712">m)</span> from the LM to take photographs at the rim of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_West_(lunar_crater)" title="Little West (lunar crater)" id="mwBgk">Little West Crater</a><!-- There is no "East Crater", see https://history.nasa.gov/alsj/a11/a11EastCraterRIP.html --> while Aldrin collected two <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_sample" title="Core sample" id="mwBgo">core samples</a>.
