He used the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geologist's_hammer" title="Geologist's hammer" id="mwBgs">geologist's hammer</a> to pound in the tubes—the only time the hammer was used on Apollo 11—but was unable to penetrate more than <span about="#mwt713" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBgw" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;6&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;in&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;cm&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">6 inches (15</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt713">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt713">cm)</span> deep. The astronauts then collected rock samples using scoops and tongs on extension handles.<sup about="#mwt714" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29_161-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29-161&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Harland&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1999&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;28–29&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29-161" id="mwBg0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBg4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBg8">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBhE">Many of the surface activities took longer than expected, so they had to stop documenting sample collection halfway through the allotted 34 minutes. Aldrin shoveled <span about="#mwt718" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBhI" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;6&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;kg&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">6 kilograms (13</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt718">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt718">lb)</span> of soil into the box of rocks to pack them in tightly.<sup about="#mwt719" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29_161-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29-161&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Harland&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1999&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;28–29&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarland199928–29-161" id="mwBhM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBhQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhU">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhY">]</span></span></a></sup> Two types of rocks were found in the geological samples: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basalt" title="Basalt" id="mwBhc">basalt</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breccia" title="Breccia" id="mwBhg">breccia</a>.<sup about="#mwt724" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-162" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-162&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-162" id="mwBhk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBho"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhs">[</span>160<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBhw">]</span></span></a></sup> Three new minerals were discovered in the rock samples collected by the astronauts: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armalcolite" title="Armalcolite" id="mwBh0">armalcolite</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranquillityite" title="Tranquillityite" id="mwBh4">tranquillityite</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyroxferroite" title="Pyroxferroite" id="mwBh8">pyroxferroite</a>. Armalcolite was named after Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins. All have subsequently been found on Earth.<sup about="#mwt727" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-163" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-163&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-163" id="mwBiA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBiE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBiI">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBiM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBiQ"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_plaque_closeup_on_Moon.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBiU"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_plaque_closeup_on_Moon.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Apollo_11_plaque_closeup_on_Moon.jpg/250px-Apollo_11_plaque_closeup_on_Moon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Apollo_11_plaque_closeup_on_Moon.jpg/500px-Apollo_11_plaque_closeup_on_Moon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="873" data-file-height="822" data-file-type="bitmap" height="235" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBiY"></a><figcaption id="mwBic"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_plaque" title="Lunar plaque" id="mwBig">The plaque</a> left on the ladder of <i id="mwBik">Eagle</i></figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBio">While on the surface, Armstrong uncovered a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_plaque" title="Lunar plaque" id="mwBis">plaque</a> mounted on the LM ladder, bearing two drawings of Earth (of the Western and Eastern Hemispheres), an inscription, and signatures of the astronauts and President Nixon. The inscription read:</p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt728" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwBiw" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon July 1969, A. &lt;!-- actual plaque clearly includes a space here --&gt;D. We came in peace for all mankind.&lt;ref name=\&quot;ALSJ 4\&quot; /&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt728" id="mwBi0"><p>Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon July 1969, A. D. We came in peace for all mankind.<sup about="#mwt730" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_4_142-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 4&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_4-142" id="mwBi4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBi8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjA">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjE">]</span></span></a></sup></p></blockquote>

<p id="mwBjI">At the behest of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon_administration" title="Nixon administration" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBjM">Nixon administration</a> to add a reference to God, NASA included the vague date as a reason to include A.D., which stands for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anno_Domini" title="Anno Domini" id="mwBjQ">Anno Domini</a> ("in the year of our Lord").<sup about="#mwt732" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGardner2017143_164-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEGardner2017143&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEGardner2017143-164&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Gardner&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2017&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;143&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGardner2017143-164" id="mwBjU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBjY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjc">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBjk">Mission Control used a coded phrase to warn Armstrong his metabolic rates were high, and that he should slow down. He was moving rapidly from task to task as time ran out. As metabolic rates remained generally lower than expected for both astronauts throughout the walk, Mission Control granted the astronauts a 15-minute extension.<sup about="#mwt737" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-EASEP_Deployment_and_Closeout_160-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;EASEP Deployment and Closeout&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-EASEP_Deployment_and_Closeout-160&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-EASEP_Deployment_and_Closeout-160" id="mwBjo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBjs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBjw">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBj0">]</span></span></a></sup> In a 2010 interview, Armstrong explained that NASA limited the first moonwalk's time and distance because there was no empirical proof of how much cooling water the astronauts' PLSS backpacks would consume to handle their body heat generation while working on the Moon.<sup about="#mwt740" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-165" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-165&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-165" id="mwBj4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBj8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkA">[</span>163<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="21" id="mwBkI" aria-labelledby="Lunar_ascent"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Lunar_ascent">Lunar ascent</h3></div>

<p id="mwBkM">Aldrin entered <i id="mwBkQ">Eagle</i> first. With some difficulty the astronauts lifted film and two sample boxes containing <span about="#mwt741" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBkU" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;21.55&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;kg&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;lb&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">21.55 kilograms (47.5</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt741">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt741">lb)</span> of lunar surface material to the LM hatch using a flat cable pulley device called the Lunar Equipment Conveyor (LEC). This proved to be an inefficient tool, and later missions preferred to carry equipment and samples up to the LM by hand.<sup about="#mwt742" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_3_137-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 3&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_3-137" id="mwBkY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBkc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkg">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBkk">]</span></span></a></sup> Armstrong reminded Aldrin of a bag of memorial items in his sleeve pocket, and Aldrin tossed the bag down. Armstrong then jumped onto the ladder's third rung, and climbed into the LM. After transferring to LM <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_support" title="Life support" id="mwBko">life support</a>, the explorers lightened the ascent stage for the return to lunar orbit by tossing out their PLSS backpacks, lunar overshoes, an empty Hasselblad camera, and other equipment.<sup about="#mwt745" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-166" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-166&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-166" id="mwBks"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBkw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBk0">[</span>164<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBk4">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt748" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-167" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-167&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-167" id="mwBk8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBlA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlE">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlI">]</span></span></a></sup> The hatch was closed again at 05:11:13. They then pressurized the LM and settled down to sleep.<sup about="#mwt751" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_6_168-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 6&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ALSJ_6-168&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_6-168" id="mwBlM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBlQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlU">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBlc"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aldrin_Looks_Back_at_Tranquility_Base_-_GPN-2000-001102.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBlg"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aldrin_Looks_Back_at_Tranquility_Base_-_GPN-2000-001102.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Aldrin_Looks_Back_at_Tranquility_Base_-_GPN-2000-001102.jpg/500px-Aldrin_Looks_Back_at_Tranquility_Base_-_GPN-2000-001102.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Aldrin_Looks_Back_at_Tranquility_Base_-_GPN-2000-001102.jpg/960px-Aldrin_Looks_Back_at_Tranquility_Base_-_GPN-2000-001102.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3904" data-file-height="3904" data-file-type="bitmap" height="350" width="350" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.4" id="mwBlk"></a><figcaption id="mwBlo">Aldrin next to the Passive Seismic Experiment Package with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module" title="Apollo Lunar Module" id="mwBls">Lunar Module</a> <i id="mwBlw">Eagle</i> in the background</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBl0">Presidential speech writer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Safire" title="William Safire" id="mwBl4">William Safire</a> had prepared an <i id="mwBl8">In Event of Moon Disaster</i> announcement for Nixon to read in the event the Apollo 11 astronauts were stranded on the Moon.<sup about="#mwt754" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-169" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-169&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-169" id="mwBmA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBmE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmI">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmM">]</span></span></a></sup> The remarks were in a memo from Safire to Nixon's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Chief_of_Staff" title="White House Chief of Staff" id="mwBmQ">White House Chief of Staff</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._R._Haldeman" title="H. R. Haldeman" id="mwBmU">H. R. Haldeman</a>, in which Safire suggested a protocol the administration might follow in reaction to such a disaster.<sup about="#mwt757" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-170" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-170&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-170" id="mwBmY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBmc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmg">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt760" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-safire_171-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;safire&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-safire-171&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-safire-171" id="mwBmo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBms"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmw">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBm0">]</span></span></a></sup> According to the plan, Mission Control would "close down communications" with the LM, and a clergyman would "commend their souls to the deepest of the deep" in a public ritual likened to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burial_at_sea" title="Burial at sea" id="mwBm4">burial at sea</a>. The last line of the prepared text contained an allusion to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Brooke" title="Rupert Brooke" id="mwBm8">Rupert Brooke</a>'s World War I poem "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Soldier_(poem)" title="The Soldier (poem)" id="mwBnA">The Soldier</a>".<sup about="#mwt761" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-safire_171-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;safire&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-safire-171" id="mwBnE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBnI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnM">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The script for the speech does not make reference to Collins; as he remained onboard <i id="mwBnU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_module_Columbia" title="Command module Columbia" id="mwBnY">Columbia</a></i> in orbit around the Moon, it was expected that he would be able to return the module to Earth in the event of a mission failure.<sup about="#mwt764" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-172" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-172&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-172" id="mwBnc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBng"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnk">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBno">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBns">While moving inside the cabin, Aldrin accidentally damaged the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_breaker" title="Circuit breaker" id="mwBnw">circuit breaker</a> that would arm the main engine for liftoff from the Moon. There was a concern this would prevent firing the engine, stranding them on the Moon. The nonconductive tip of a Duro <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marker_pen" title="Marker pen" id="mwBn0">felt-tip pen</a><sup about="#mwt767" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-173" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-173&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-173" id="mwBn4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBn8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoA">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoE">]</span></span></a></sup> was sufficient to activate the switch.<sup about="#mwt768" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_6_168-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ 6&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_6-168" id="mwBoI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBoM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoQ">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBoY">After more than <style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1154941027" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" about="#mwt769" id="mwBoc" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Fraction/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;frac&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Frac&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;21&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">.mw-parser-output .frac{white-space:nowrap}.mw-parser-output .frac .num,.mw-parser-output .frac .den{font-size:80%;line-height:0;vertical-align:super}.mw-parser-output .frac .den{vertical-align:sub}.mw-parser-output .sr-only{border:0;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);clip-path:polygon(0px 0px,0px 0px,0px 0px);height:1px;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px}</style><span class="frac" about="#mwt769" id="mwBog">21<span class="sr-only">+</span><span class="num">1</span><span typeof="mw:Entity">⁄</span><span class="den">2</span></span> hours on the lunar surface, in addition to the scientific instruments, the astronauts left behind: an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_1" title="Apollo 1" id="mwBok">Apollo 1</a> mission patch in memory of astronauts<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBoo">&nbsp;</span><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_B._Chaffee" title="Roger B. Chaffee" id="mwBos">Roger Chaffee</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Grissom" title="Gus Grissom" id="mwBow">Gus Grissom</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_White_(astronaut)" title="Ed White (astronaut)" id="mwBo0">Edward White</a>, who died when their command module caught fire during a test in January 1967; two memorial medals of Soviet cosmonauts <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Komarov" title="Vladimir Komarov" id="mwBo4">Vladimir Komarov</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Gagarin" title="Yuri Gagarin" id="mwBo8">Yuri Gagarin</a>, who died in 1967 and 1968 respectively; a memorial bag containing a gold replica of an olive branch as a traditional symbol of peace; and a silicon message disk carrying the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_goodwill_messages" title="Apollo 11 goodwill messages" id="mwBpA">goodwill statements</a> by presidents Eisenhower, Kennedy, Johnson, and Nixon along with messages from leaders of 73 countries around the world.<sup about="#mwt773" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-174" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-174&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-174" id="mwBpE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpM">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The disk also carries a listing of the leadership of the US Congress, a listing of members of the four committees of the House and Senate responsible for the NASA legislation, and the names of NASA's past and then-current top management.<sup about="#mwt776" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-175" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-175&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-175" id="mwBpU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpc">[</span>173<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBpk"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_photo_map.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBpo"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_photo_map.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Apollo_11_photo_map.svg/330px-Apollo_11_photo_map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Apollo_11_photo_map.svg/960px-Apollo_11_photo_map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="709" data-file-height="709" data-file-type="drawing" height="330" width="330" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.3" id="mwBps"></a><figcaption id="mwBpw">A map of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranquility_Base" title="Tranquility Base" id="mwBp0">Tranquility Base</a> landing site and photos taken</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBp4">After about seven hours of rest, the crew was awakened by Houston to prepare for the return flight.
At that time, unknown to them, some hundred kilometers away from them the Soviet probe <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_15" title="Luna 15" id="mwBp8">Luna 15</a> was about to descend and impact. Despite having been known to be orbiting the Moon at the same time, through a ground-breaking precautious goodwill exchange of data, the mission control of Luna 15 unexpectedly hastened its robotic <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sample-return_mission" title="Sample-return mission" id="mwBqA">sample-return mission</a>, initiating descent, in an attempt to return before Apollo 11.<sup about="#mwt779" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-audio_176-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;audio&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-audio-176&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-audio-176" id="mwBqE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqM">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Just two hours before Apollo 11's launch, Luna 15 crashed at 15:50 UTC, with British astronomers monitoring Luna 15 and recording the situation one commented: "I say, this has really been drama of the highest order",<sup about="#mwt782" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-a357_177-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;a357&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-a357-177&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-a357-177" id="mwBqU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqc">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqg">]</span></span></a></sup> bringing the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race" title="Space Race" id="mwBqk">Space Race</a> to a culmination.<sup about="#mwt785" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-178" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-178&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-178" id="mwBqo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqw">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBq0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBq4">Roughly two hours later, at 17:54:00 UTC, the Apollo 11 crew on the surface safely lifted off in <i id="mwBq8">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt786" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBrA" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> ascent stage to rejoin Collins aboard <i id="mwBrE">Columbia</i> in lunar orbit.<sup about="#mwt787" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108_148-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108-148&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;108&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000108-148" id="mwBrI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBrM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrQ">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrU">]</span></span></a></sup> Film taken from the LM ascent stage upon liftoff from the Moon reveals the American flag, planted some <span about="#mwt790" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBrY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;25&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;0&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">25 feet (8</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt790">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt790">m)</span> from the descent stage, whipping violently in the exhaust of the ascent stage engine. Aldrin looked up in time to witness the flag topple: "The ascent stage of the LM separated<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBrc">&nbsp;</span>... I was concentrating on the computers, and Neil was studying the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attitude_indicator" title="Attitude indicator" id="mwBrg">attitude indicator</a>, but I looked up long enough to see the flag fall over."<sup about="#mwt791" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975219_179-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975219&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975219-179&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Aldrin&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1975&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;219&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975219-179" id="mwBrk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBro"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrs">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrw">]</span></span></a></sup> Subsequent Apollo missions planted their flags farther from the LM.<sup about="#mwt796" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-180" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-180&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-180" id="mwBr0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBr4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBr8">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="22" id="mwBsE" aria-labelledby="Columbia_in_lunar_orbit"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Columbia_in_lunar_orbit"><i id="mwBsI">Columbia</i> in lunar orbit</h3></div>

<p id="mwBsM">During his day flying solo around the Moon, Collins never felt lonely. Although it has been said "not since <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam" title="Adam" id="mwBsQ">Adam</a> has any human known such solitude",<sup about="#mwt797" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001402_181-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001402&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001402-181&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;402&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001402-181" id="mwBsU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBsY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsc">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsg">]</span></span></a></sup> Collins felt very much a part of the mission. In his autobiography he wrote: "this venture has been structured for three men, and I consider my third to be as necessary as either of the other two".<sup about="#mwt800" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001402_181-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001402&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001402-181&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;402&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001402-181" id="mwBsk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBso"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBss">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBsw">]</span></span></a></sup> In the 48 minutes of each orbit when he was out of radio contact with the Earth while <i id="mwBs0">Columbia</i> passed round the far side of the Moon, the feeling he reported was not fear or loneliness, but rather "awareness, anticipation, satisfaction, confidence, almost exultation".<sup about="#mwt803" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001402_181-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001402&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001402-181&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;402&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001402-181" id="mwBs4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBs8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtA">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBtI">One of Collins' first tasks was to identify the Lunar Module on the ground. To give Collins an idea where to look, Mission Control radioed that they believed the Lunar Module landed about <span about="#mwt806" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBtM" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;4&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;mile&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;km&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">4 miles (6.4</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt806">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt806">km)</span> off target. Each time he passed over the suspected lunar landing site, he tried in vain to find the module. On his first orbits on the back side of the Moon, Collins performed maintenance activities such as dumping excess water produced by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuel_cell" title="Fuel cell" id="mwBtQ">fuel cells</a> and preparing the cabin for Armstrong and Aldrin to return.<sup about="#mwt807" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001401–407_182-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001401–407&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001401–407-182&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;401–407&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001401–407-182" id="mwBtU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtc">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBtk">Just before he reached the dark side on the third orbit, Mission Control informed Collins there was a problem with the temperature of the coolant. If it became too cold, parts of <i id="mwBto">Columbia</i> might freeze. Mission Control advised him to assume manual control and implement Environmental Control System Malfunction Procedure 17. Instead, Collins flicked the switch on the system from automatic to manual and back to automatic again, and carried on with normal housekeeping chores, while keeping an eye on the temperature.<sup about="#mwt810" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408,_410_183-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408, 410&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408,_410-183&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;406–408, 410&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408,_410-183" id="mwBts"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBt0">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBt4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBt8">When <i id="mwBuA">Columbia</i> came back around to the near side of the Moon again, Collins was able to report that the problem had been resolved. For the next couple of orbits, he described his time on the back side of the Moon as "relaxing". After Aldrin and Armstrong completed their EVA, Collins slept so he could be rested for the rendezvous. While the flight plan called for <i id="mwBuE">Eagle</i> to meet up with <i id="mwBuI">Columbia</i>, Collins was prepared for a contingency in which he would fly <i id="mwBuM">Columbia</i> down to meet <i id="mwBuQ">Eagle</i>.<sup about="#mwt813" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408,_410_183-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408, 410&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408,_410-183&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;406–408, 410&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollins2001406–408,_410-183" id="mwBuU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBuY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuc">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBug">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="23" id="mwBuk" aria-labelledby="Return"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Return">Return</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBuo"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Earth,_Moon_and_Lunar_Module,_AS11-44-6643_c.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBus"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Earth,_Moon_and_Lunar_Module,_AS11-44-6643_c.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Earth%2C_Moon_and_Lunar_Module%2C_AS11-44-6643_c.jpg/250px-Earth%2C_Moon_and_Lunar_Module%2C_AS11-44-6643_c.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Earth%2C_Moon_and_Lunar_Module%2C_AS11-44-6643_c.jpg/500px-Earth%2C_Moon_and_Lunar_Module%2C_AS11-44-6643_c.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="4161" data-file-height="3980" data-file-type="bitmap" height="239" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwBuw"></a><figcaption id="mwBu0"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Module_Eagle" title="Lunar Module Eagle" id="mwBu4"><i id="mwBu8">Eagle</i></a><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt816" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBvA" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> ascent stage approaching <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_Module_Columbia" title="Command Module Columbia" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBvE"><i id="mwBvI">Columbia</i></a></figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwBvM"><i id="mwBvQ">Eagle</i> rendezvoused with <i id="mwBvU">Columbia</i> at 21:24 UTC on July 21, and the two docked at 21:35. <i id="mwBvY">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt817" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBvc" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span></span>s ascent stage was jettisoned into lunar orbit at 23:41.<sup about="#mwt818" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000109_9-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEOrloff2000109&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000109-9&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Orloff&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2000&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;109&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff2000109-9" id="mwBvg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBvk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvo">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvs">]</span></span></a></sup> Just before the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_12" title="Apollo 12" id="mwBvw">Apollo 12</a> flight, it was noted that <i id="mwBv0">Eagle</i> was still likely to be orbiting the Moon. Later NASA reports mentioned that <i id="mwBv4">Eagle</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt821" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBv8" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'s&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'s&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span>s</span> orbit had decayed, resulting in it impacting in an "uncertain location" on the lunar surface.<sup about="#mwt824" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-184" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-184&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-184" id="mwBwA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBwE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwI">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwM">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2021, however, some calculations show that the lander may still be in orbit.<sup about="#mwt827" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-185" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-185&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-185" id="mwBwQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBwU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwY">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBwg">On July 23, the last night before splashdown, the three astronauts made a television broadcast in which Collins commented: "All this is possible only through the blood, sweat, and tears of a number of people<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBwk">&nbsp;</span>... All you see is the three of us, but beneath the surface are thousands and thousands of others, and to all of those, I would like to say, 'Thank you very much'."<sup about="#mwt828" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222_186-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222-186&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Aldrin&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1975&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;222&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222-186" id="mwBwo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBws"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBww">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBw0">]</span></span></a></sup> Aldrin added: "This has been far more than three men on a mission to the Moon; more, still, than the efforts of a government and industry team; more, even, than the efforts of one nation. We feel that this stands as a symbol of the insatiable curiosity of all mankind to explore the unknown<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwBw4">&nbsp;</span>..."<sup about="#mwt831" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222_186-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222-186&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Collins&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Aldrin&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1975&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;222&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222-186" id="mwBw8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxE">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBxM">Armstrong concluded:</p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt834" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwBxQ" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;The responsibility for this flight lies first with history and with the giants of science who have preceded this effort; next with the American people, who have, through their will, indicated their desire; next with four administrations and their Congresses, for implementing that will; and then, with the agency and industry teams that built our spacecraft, the Saturn, the Columbia, the Eagle, and the little [[Extravehicular Mobility Unit|EMU]], the spacesuit and backpack that was our small spacecraft out on the lunar surface. We would like to give special thanks to all those Americans who built the spacecraft; who did the construction, design, the tests, and put their hearts and all their abilities into those craft. To those people tonight, we give a special thank you, and to all the other people that are listening and watching tonight, God bless you. Good night from Apollo 11.{{sfn|Collins|Aldrin|1975|p=222}} &quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt834" id="mwBxU"><p>The responsibility for this flight lies first with history and with the giants of science who have preceded this effort; next with the American people, who have, through their will, indicated their desire; next with four administrations and their Congresses, for implementing that will; and then, with the agency and industry teams that built our spacecraft, the Saturn, the Columbia, the Eagle, and the little <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extravehicular_Mobility_Unit" title="Extravehicular Mobility Unit">EMU</a>, the spacesuit and backpack that was our small spacecraft out on the lunar surface. We would like to give special thanks to all those Americans who built the spacecraft; who did the construction, design, the tests, and put their hearts and all their abilities into those craft. To those people tonight, we give a special thank you, and to all the other people that are listening and watching tonight, God bless you. Good night from Apollo 11.<sup about="#mwt836" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222_186-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222-186&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECollinsAldrin1975222-186" id="mwBxY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxg">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxk">]</span></span></a></sup> </p></blockquote>

<p id="mwBxo">On the return to Earth, a bearing at the Guam tracking station failed, potentially preventing communication on the last segment of the Earth return. A regular repair was not possible in the available time but the station director, Charles Force, had his ten-year-old son Greg use his small hands to reach into the housing and pack it with grease. Greg was later thanked by Armstrong.<sup about="#mwt840" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-187" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-187&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-187" id="mwBxs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBx0">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBx4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="24" id="mwBx8" aria-labelledby="Splashdown_and_quarantine"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Splashdown_and_quarantine">Splashdown and quarantine</h3></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwByA"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Splashdown_3.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwByE"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Splashdown_3.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Splashdown_3.jpg/250px-Splashdown_3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Splashdown_3.jpg/500px-Splashdown_3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="1179" data-file-height="1131" data-file-type="bitmap" height="240" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwByI"></a><figcaption id="mwByM"><i id="mwByQ">Columbia</i> floats on the ocean as Navy divers assist in retrieving the astronauts.</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwByU">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier" title="Aircraft carrier" id="mwByY">aircraft carrier</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Hornet_(CV-12)" title="USS Hornet (CV-12)" about="#mwt841" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwByc" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;USS&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:USS&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hornet&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;CV-12&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;6&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">USS<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span><i>Hornet</i></a>, under the command of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-6)" title="Captain (United States O-6)" id="mwByg">Captain</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_J._Seiberlich" title="Carl J. Seiberlich" id="mwByk">Carl J. Seiberlich</a>,<sup about="#mwt842" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael20103_188-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael20103&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael20103-188&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;3&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael20103-188" id="mwByo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBys"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwByw">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBy0">]</span></span></a></sup> was selected as the primary recovery ship (PRS) for Apollo 11 on June 5, replacing her sister ship, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landing_platform_helicopter" title="Landing platform helicopter" id="mwBy4">LPH</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Princeton_(CV-37)" title="USS Princeton (CV-37)" about="#mwt845" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBy8" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;USS&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:USS&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Princeton&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;CV-37&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;6&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">USS<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span><i>Princeton</i></a>, which had recovered Apollo 10 on May 26. <i id="mwBzA">Hornet</i> was then at her home port of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Beach,_California" title="Long Beach, California" id="mwBzE">Long Beach, California</a>.<sup about="#mwt846" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael201021_189-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael201021&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael201021-189&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;21&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael201021-189" id="mwBzI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBzM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzQ">[</span>187<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzU">]</span></span></a></sup> On reaching <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Harbor" title="Pearl Harbor" id="mwBzY">Pearl Harbor</a> on July 5, <i id="mwBzc">Hornet</i> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embarkation" title="Embarkation" id="mwBzg">embarked</a> the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" representatives. To make room, most of <i id="mwBzw">Hornet</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt849" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBz0" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span></span>s air wing was left behind in Long Beach. Special recovery equipment was also loaded, including a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boilerplate_(spaceflight)" title="Boilerplate (spaceflight)" id="mwBz4">boilerplate</a> command module used for training.<sup about="#mwt850" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael201038–43,_71–72_190-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael201038–43, 71–72&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael201038–43,_71–72-190&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;38–43, 71–72&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael201038–43,_71–72-190" id="mwBz8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB0A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0E">[</span>188<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0I">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB0M">On July 12, with Apollo 11 still on the launch pad, <i id="mwB0Q">Hornet</i> departed Pearl Harbor for the recovery area in the central Pacific,<sup about="#mwt853" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael201085_191-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael201085&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael201085-191&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;85&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a After a night on board, they would fly to <i id="mwB1c">Hornet</i> in Marine One for a few hours of ceremonies. On arrival aboard <i id="mwB1g">Hornet</i>, the party was greeted by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Indo-Pacific_Command" title="United States Indo-Pacific Command" id="mwB1k">Commander-in-Chief, Pacific Command (CINCPAC)</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiral_(United_States)" title="Admiral (United States)" id="mwB1o">Admiral</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_S._McCain_Jr." title="John S. <p id="mwB2c">Weather satellites were not yet common, but US Air Force <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-3)" title="Captain (United States O-3)" id="mwB2g">Captain</a> Hank Brandli had access to top-secret <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CORONA_(satellite)" title="CORONA (satellite)" id="mwB2k">spy satellite</a> images. He realized that a storm front was headed for the Apollo recovery area. Poor visibility which could make locating the capsule difficult, and strong upper-level winds which "would have ripped their parachutes to shreds" according to Brandli, posed a serious threat to the safety of the mission.<sup about="#mwt871" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-194" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-194&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-194" id="mwB2o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2w">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB20">]</span></span></a></sup> Brandli alerted Navy Captain Willard S. Houston Jr., the commander of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Typhoon_Warning_Center" title="Joint Typhoon Warning Center" id="mwB24">Fleet Weather Center</a> at Pearl Harbor, who had the required security clearance. On their recommendation, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_admiral_(United_States)" title="Rear admiral (United States)" id="mwB28">Rear Admiral</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_C._Davis" title="Donald C. Davis" id="mwB3A">Donald C. Davis</a>, commander of Manned Spaceflight Recovery Forces, Pacific, advised NASA to change the recovery area, each man risking his career. A new location was selected <span about="#mwt865" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB3E" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;215&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;nmi&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;km&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">215 nautical miles (398</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt865">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt865">km)</span> northeast.<sup about="#mwt872" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_Re-entry_195-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ Re-entry&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_Re-entry-195" id="mwB3I"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3M"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3Q">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3U">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt866" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010136–137,_144–145_196-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael2010136–137, 144–145&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010136–137,_144–145-196&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;136–137, 144–145&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010136–137,_144–145-196" id="mwB3Y"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3c"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3g">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3k">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB3o">This altered the flight plan. A different sequence of computer programs was used, one never before attempted. In a conventional entry, trajectory event P64 was followed by P67. For a skip-out re-entry, P65 and P66 were employed to handle the exit and entry parts of the skip. In this case, because they were extending the re-entry but not actually skipping out, P66 was not invoked and instead, P65 led directly to P67. The crew were also warned they would not be in a full-lift (heads-down) attitude when they entered P67.<sup about="#mwt880" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ALSJ_Re-entry_195-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ALSJ Re-entry&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ALSJ_Re-entry-195&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ALSJ_Re-entry-195" id="mwB3s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB30">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB34">]</span></span></a></sup> The first program's acceleration subjected the astronauts to <span about="#mwt873" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB38" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;6.5&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;g0&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">6.5 standard gravities (64</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt873">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt873">m/s</span><sup about="#mwt873">2</sup><span about="#mwt873">)</span>; the second, to <span about="#mwt874" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB4A" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;6.0&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;g0&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">6.0 standard gravities (59</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt874">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt874">m/s</span><sup about="#mwt874">2</sup><span about="#mwt874">)</span>.<sup about="#mwt875" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196928_197-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team196928&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196928-197&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;28&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team196928-197" id="mwB4E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4M">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB4U">Before dawn on July 24, <i id="mwB4Y">Hornet</i> launched four Sea King helicopters and three <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_E-1_Tracer" title="Grumman E-1 Tracer" id="mwB4c">Grumman E-1 Tracers</a>. Two of the E-1s were designated as "air boss" while the third acted as a communications relay aircraft. Two of the Sea Kings carried divers and recovery equipment. The third carried photographic equipment, and the fourth carried the decontamination swimmer and the flight surgeon.<sup about="#mwt881" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969169–170_198-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team1969169–170&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969169–170-198&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;169–170&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969169–170-198" id="mwB4g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4k"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4o">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4s">]</span></span></a></sup> At 16:44 UTC (05:44 local time) <i id="mwB4w">Columbia</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;" about="#mwt884" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB40" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;'&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">'</span></span>s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drogue_parachute" title="Drogue parachute" id="mwB44">drogue parachutes</a> were deployed. This was observed by the helicopters. Seven minutes later <i id="mwB48">Columbia</i> struck the water forcefully <span about="#mwt885" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB5A" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2660&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;km&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;nmi&quot;},&quot;abbr&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;on&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">2,660</span><span <p id="mwB68">During <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splashdown" title="Splashdown" id="mwB7A">splashdown</a>, <i id="mwB7E">Columbia</i> landed upside down but was righted within ten minutes by flotation bags activated by the astronauts.<sup about="#mwt908" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969164–167_202-0" rel="dc:references" anchor</a> to prevent it from drifting.<sup about="#mwt911" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010184–185_203-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref"
