<p id="mwB8A">The divers then passed biological isolation garments (BIGs) to the astronauts, and assisted them into the life raft. The possibility of bringing back <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen" title="Pathogen" id="mwB8E">pathogens</a> from the lunar surface was considered remote, but NASA took precautions at the recovery site. The astronauts were rubbed down with a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium_hypochlorite" title="Sodium hypochlorite" id="mwB8I">sodium hypochlorite</a> solution and <i id="mwB8M">Columbia</i> wiped with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Povidone-iodine" title="Povidone-iodine" id="mwB8Q">povidone-iodine</a> to remove any lunar dust that might be present. The astronauts were winched on board the recovery helicopter. BIGs were worn until they reached isolation facilities on board <i id="mwB8U">Hornet</i>. The raft containing decontamination materials was intentionally sunk.<sup about="#mwt919" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969164–167_202-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team1969164–167&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969164–167-202&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;164–167&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969164–167-202" id="mwB8Y"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB8c"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8g">[</span>200<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8k">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB8o">After touchdown on <i id="mwB8s">Hornet</i> at 17:53 UTC, the helicopter was lowered by the elevator into the hangar bay, where the astronauts walked the <span about="#mwt922" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB8w" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;30&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;m&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">30 feet (9.1</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt922">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt922">m)</span> to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_quarantine_facility" title="Mobile quarantine facility" id="mwB80">mobile quarantine facility</a> (MQF), where they would begin the Earth-based portion of their 21 days of quarantine.<sup about="#mwt923" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010199–200_205-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael2010199–200&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010199–200-205&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;199–200&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010199–200-205" id="mwB84"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB88"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9A">[</span>203<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9E">]</span></span></a></sup> This practice would continue for two more Apollo missions, Apollo 12 and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_14" title="Apollo 14" id="mwB9I">Apollo 14</a>, before the Moon was proven to be barren of life, and the quarantine process dropped.<sup about="#mwt926" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975406–424_206-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975406–424&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975406–424-206&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Johnston&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Dietlein&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Berry&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1975&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;406–424&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJohnstonDietleinBerry1975406–424-206" id="mwB9M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB9Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9U">[</span>204<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9Y">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt931" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-207" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-207&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-207" id="mwB9c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB9g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9k">[</span>205<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9o">]</span></span></a></sup> Nixon welcomed the astronauts back to Earth. He told them: "[A]<!-- lowercase in source -->s a result of what you've done, the world has never been closer together before."<sup about="#mwt934" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-208" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-208&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-208" id="mwB9s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB9w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB90">[</span>206<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB94">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB98">After Nixon departed, <i id="mwB-A">Hornet</i> was brought alongside the <span about="#mwt935" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB-E" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;5&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ST&quot;},&quot;adj&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;on&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">5-short-ton (4.5</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt935">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt935">t)</span> <i id="mwB-I">Columbia</i>, which was lifted aboard by the ship's crane, placed on a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_(trailer)" title="Dolly (trailer)" id="mwB-M">dolly</a> and moved next to the MQF. It was then attached to the MQF with a flexible tunnel,<sup about="#mwt936" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969166,_171–173_209-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team1969166, 171–173&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969166,_171–173-209&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;166, 171–173&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969166,_171–173-209" id="mwB-Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB-U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-Y">[</span>207<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-c">]</span></span></a></sup> allowing the lunar samples, film, data tapes and other items to be removed by MQF project engineer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hirasaki" title="John Hirasaki" id="mwB-g">John Hirasaki</a>. He placed the two <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Sample_Return_Container" title="Apollo Lunar Sample Return Container" id="mwB-k">Apollo Lunar Sample Return Containers</a> (ALSRC) containing lunar samples, space suits and film cassettes into plastic bags. Hirasaki then passed the bags out of the MQF through a transfer lock with a decontamination wash. All of the collected materials were flown to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellington_Air_Force_Base" title="Ellington Air Force Base" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB-o">Ellington Air Force Base</a> in Houston and taken to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Receiving_Laboratory" title="Lunar Receiving Laboratory" id="mwB-s">Lunar Receiving Laboratory</a> (LRL) within 48 hours of splashdown.<sup about="#mwt941" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-210" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-210&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-210" id="mwB-w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB-0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-4">[</span>208<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB_A"><i id="mwB_E">Hornet</i> returned to Pearl Harbor on July 26, where it was welcomed by thousands of people. The MQF was loaded onto a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_C-141_Starlifter" title="Lockheed C-141 Starlifter" id="mwB_I">Lockheed C-141 Starlifter</a> at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hickam_Air_Force_Base" title="Hickam Air Force Base" id="mwB_M">Hickam Air Force Base</a> and airlifted to Houston, landing on July 27.<sup about="#mwt947" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-211" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-211&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-211" id="mwB_Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB_U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_Y">[</span>209<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_c">]</span></span></a></sup> The astronauts arrived at the LRL at 10:00 UTC on July 28. <i id="mwB_g">Columbia</i> was taken to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Island" title="Ford Island" id="mwB_k">Ford Island</a> for deactivation, and its pyrotechnics made safe. It was then taken to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hickham_Air_Force_Base" title="Hickham Air Force Base" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB_o">Hickham Air Force Base</a>, from whence it was flown to Houston in a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_C-133_Cargomaster" title="Douglas C-133 Cargomaster" id="mwB_s">Douglas C-133 Cargomaster</a>, reaching the Lunar Receiving Laboratory on July 30.<sup about="#mwt942" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969166,_171–173_209-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMission Evaluation Team1969166, 171–173&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969166,_171–173-209&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Mission Evaluation Team&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1969&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;166, 171–173&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMission_Evaluation_Team1969166,_171–173-209" id="mwB_w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB_0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_4">[</span>207<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCAA">In accordance with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra-Terrestrial_Exposure_Law" title="Extra-Terrestrial Exposure Law" id="mwCAE">Extra-Terrestrial Exposure Law</a>, a set of regulations promulgated by NASA on July 16 to codify its quarantine protocol,<sup about="#mwt955" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-212" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-212&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-212" id="mwCAI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAQ">[</span>210<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAU">]</span></span></a></sup> the astronauts continued in quarantine. After three weeks in confinement (first in the Apollo spacecraft, then in their trailer on <i id="mwCAY">Hornet</i>, and finally in the Lunar Receiving Laboratory), the astronauts were given a clean bill of health.<sup about="#mwt958" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-213" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-213&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-213" id="mwCAc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAk">[</span>211<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAo">]</span></span></a></sup> On August 10, 1969, the Interagency Committee on Back Contamination met in Atlanta and lifted the quarantine on the astronauts, on those who had joined them in quarantine (NASA physician <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Carpentier" title="William Carpentier" id="mwCAs">William Carpentier</a> and John Hirasaki),<sup about="#mwt948" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010118_214-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECarmichael2010118&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010118-214&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Carmichael&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;118&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarmichael2010118-214" id="mwCAw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCA0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCA4">[</span>212<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCA8">]</span></span></a></sup> and on <i id="mwCBA">Columbia</i> itself. Loose equipment from the spacecraft remained in isolation until the lunar samples were released for study.<sup about="#mwt951" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEErtelNewkirkBrooks1978312_215-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEErtelNewkirkBrooks1978312&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEErtelNewkirkBrooks1978312-215&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Ertel&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Newkirk&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1978&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;312&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErtelNewkirkBrooks1978312-215" id="mwCBE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCBI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBM">[</span>213<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCBU"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_ticker_tape_parade_1.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCBY"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_ticker_tape_parade_1.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Apollo_11_ticker_tape_parade_1.jpg/250px-Apollo_11_ticker_tape_parade_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Apollo_11_ticker_tape_parade_1.jpg/500px-Apollo_11_ticker_tape_parade_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2842" data-file-height="1997" data-file-type="bitmap" height="176" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCBc"></a><figcaption id="mwCBg">August 13, 1969, New York City</figcaption></figure>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="25" id="mwCBk" aria-labelledby="Celebrations"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Celebrations">Celebrations</h2></div>
<p id="mwCBo">Following their return to Earth, the Apollo 11 crew received widespread international acclaim. On August 13, 1969, astronauts <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armstrong" title="Neil Armstrong" id="mwCBs">Neil Armstrong</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buzz_Aldrin" title="Buzz Aldrin" id="mwCBw">Buzz Aldrin</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Collins_(astronaut)" title="Michael Collins (astronaut)" id="mwCB0">Michael Collins</a> were honored with ticker-tape parades in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City" id="mwCB4">New York City</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago" title="Chicago" id="mwCB8">Chicago</a>, with an estimated six million people lining the streets.<sup about="#mwt961" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-nyc-chicago_216-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;nyc-chicago&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-nyc-chicago-216&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-nyc-chicago-216" id="mwCCA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCCE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCI">[</span>214<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCM">]</span></span></a></sup> In New York the parade started at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_Green_(New_York_City)" title="Bowling Green (New York City)" id="mwCCQ">Bowling Green</a> going down Broadway to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Hall" title="New York City Hall" id="mwCCU">City Hall</a> where Mayor <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lindsay" title="John Lindsay" id="mwCCY">John Lindsay</a> greeted them and ended at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations" title="Headquarters of the United Nations" id="mwCCc">United Nations headquarters</a>.<sup about="#mwt964" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-217" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-217&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-217" id="mwCCg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCCk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCo">[</span>215<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCs">]</span></span></a></sup> Broadway was even temporarily renamed for that day to "Apollo Way". In Chicago the parade went to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop" title="Chicago Loop" id="mwCCw">the Loop</a><sup about="#mwt967" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-218" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-218&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-218" id="mwCC0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCC4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCC8">[</span>216<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCDA">]</span></span></a></sup> and culminated at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley_Center" title="Richard J. Daley Center" id="mwCDE">Chicago Civic Center</a> where the astronauts and local officials spoke to the crowd. That evening, a state dinner was held in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles" title="Los Angeles" id="mwCDI">Los Angeles</a> at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_Plaza_Hotel" title="Century Plaza Hotel" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCDM">Century Plaza Hotel</a> to commemorate the historic achievement. The event was attended by members of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress" title="United States Congress" id="mwCDQ">Congress</a>, 44 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States)" title="Governor (United States)" id="mwCDU">state governors</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States" title="Chief Justice of the United States" id="mwCDY">Chief Justice of the United States</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_E._Burger" title="Warren E. Burger" id="mwCDc">Warren E. Burger</a> and his predecessor <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Warren" title="Earl Warren" id="mwCDg">Earl Warren</a>, as well as ambassadors from 83 nations. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States" title="President of the United States" id="mwCDk">President</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon" title="Richard Nixon" id="mwCDo">Richard Nixon</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States" title="Vice President of the United States" id="mwCDs">Vice President</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiro_Agnew" title="Spiro Agnew" id="mwCDw">Spiro Agnew</a> awarded each astronaut the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom" title="Presidential Medal of Freedom" id="mwCD0">Presidential Medal of Freedom</a>, the highest civilian honor in the United States.<sup about="#mwt970" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-state-dinner_219-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;state-dinner&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-state-dinner-219&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-state-dinner-219" id="mwCD4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCD8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEA">[</span>217<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCEI"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:New_York_City_Welcomes_the_Apollo_11_Astronauts_-_GPN-2002-000034.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCEM"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:New_York_City_Welcomes_the_Apollo_11_Astronauts_-_GPN-2002-000034.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/New_York_City_Welcomes_the_Apollo_11_Astronauts_-_GPN-2002-000034.jpg/250px-New_York_City_Welcomes_the_Apollo_11_Astronauts_-_GPN-2002-000034.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/New_York_City_Welcomes_the_Apollo_11_Astronauts_-_GPN-2002-000034.jpg/500px-New_York_City_Welcomes_the_Apollo_11_Astronauts_-_GPN-2002-000034.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2844" data-file-height="2190" data-file-type="bitmap" height="193" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCEQ"></a><figcaption id="mwCEU">Apollo 11 Astronauts - New York City - August 13, 1969</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwCEY">On September 16, the astronauts addressed a joint session of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress" title="United States Congress" id="mwCEc">Congress</a>, where they presented two <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_the_United_States" title="Flag of the United States" id="mwCEg">American flags</a>—one to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives" title="United States House of Representatives" id="mwCEk">House of Representatives</a> and one to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate" title="United States Senate" id="mwCEo">Senate</a>—that had traveled to the lunar surface aboard <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module" title="Apollo Lunar Module" id="mwCEs">Eagle</a>.<sup about="#mwt973" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-congress-flag_220-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;congress-flag&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-congress-flag-220&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-congress-flag-220" id="mwCEw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCE0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCE4">[</span>218<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCE8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCFA">One of the mission flags carried aboard the flight—the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_American_Samoa" title="Flag of American Samoa" id="mwCFE">Flag of American Samoa</a>—was later displayed at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_P._Haydon_Museum" title="Jean P. Haydon Museum" id="mwCFI">Jean P. Haydon Museum</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pago_Pago" title="Pago Pago" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCFM">Pago Pago</a>, the capital of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa" title="American Samoa" id="mwCFQ">American Samoa</a>, recognizing the territory's support role as a recovery staging area.<sup about="#mwt976" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-samoa-flag_221-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;samoa-flag&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-samoa-flag-221&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-samoa-flag-221" id="mwCFU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCFY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFc">[</span>219<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCFk"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_terrazzo.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCFo"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_terrazzo.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Apollo_terrazzo.jpg/250px-Apollo_terrazzo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Apollo_terrazzo.jpg/500px-Apollo_terrazzo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3264" data-file-height="2448" data-file-type="bitmap" height="188" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCFs"></a><figcaption id="mwCFw">Terrazzo tribute to Apollo 11 astronauts on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame" title="Hollywood Walk of Fame" id="mwCF0">Hollywood Walk of Fame</a></figcaption></figure><p id="mwCF4">Numerous countries and organizations honored the Moon landing by issuing special commemorative items. These included postage stamps, coins, medals, plaques, and magazine features. <i id="mwCF8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine)" title="Time (magazine)" id="mwCGA">TIME</a></i>, <i id="mwCGE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Geographic" title="National Geographic" id="mwCGI">National Geographic</a></i>, <i id="mwCGM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_(magazine)" title="Life (magazine)" id="mwCGQ">LIFE</a></i>, and dozens of international publications featured the astronauts on their covers. Many of these commemoratives are now held in public and private collections, and some were placed aboard later Apollo missions in symbolic tribute.<sup about="#mwt979" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-commemoratives_222-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;commemoratives&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-commemoratives-222&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-commemoratives-222" id="mwCGU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGc">[</span>220<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCGk">Additionally, the success of Apollo 11 contributed to a brief spike in interest in science and technology education, often referred to as the "Apollo effect", influencing a generation of engineers and scientists.<sup about="#mwt982" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-apollo-effect_223-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;apollo-effect&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-apollo-effect-223&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-apollo-effect-223" id="mwCGo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGw">[</span>221<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCG0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="26" id="mwCG4" aria-labelledby="World_tour"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="World_tour">World tour</h3></div>
<p id="mwCG8">The celebrations continued with a 38-day world goodwill tour titled "Giant Leap", which began on September 29 and concluded on November 5, 1969. The astronauts visited 22 countries and met with numerous heads of state, prime ministers, royalty, and civic leaders.<sup about="#mwt985" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-world-tour_224-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;world-tour&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-world-tour-224&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-world-tour-224" id="mwCHA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHI">[</span>222<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHM">]</span></span></a></sup> The tour, intended to thank the international community for their support of the space program, began in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City" id="mwCHQ">Mexico City</a> and ended in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo" title="Tokyo" id="mwCHU">Tokyo</a>.<sup about="#mwt988" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-tour-start-end_225-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;tour-start-end&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-tour-start-end-225&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-tour-start-end-225" id="mwCHY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHg">[</span>223<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHk">]</span></span></a></sup> Notable stops included <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogotá" title="Bogotá" id="mwCHo">Bogotá</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires" title="Buenos Aires" id="mwCHs">Buenos Aires</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro" title="Rio de Janeiro" id="mwCHw">Rio de Janeiro</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid" title="Madrid" id="mwCH0">Madrid</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris" title="Paris" id="mwCH4">Paris</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam" title="Amsterdam" id="mwCH8">Amsterdam</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels" title="Brussels" id="mwCIA">Brussels</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London" title="London" id="mwCIE">London</a>,<sup about="#mwt989" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-tour-itinerary_226-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;tour-itinerary&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-tour-itinerary-226" id="mwCII"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCIM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIQ">[</span>224<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIU">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Berlin" title="West Berlin" id="mwCIY">West Berlin</a>,<sup about="#mwt992" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-227" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-227&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-227" id="mwCIc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCIg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIk">[</span>225<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIo">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome" title="Rome" id="mwCIs">Rome</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade" title="Belgrade" id="mwCIw">Belgrade</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran" title="Tehran" id="mwCI0">Tehran</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai" title="Mumbai" id="mwCI4">Mumbai</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangkok" title="Bangkok" id="mwCI8">Bangkok</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney" title="Sydney" id="mwCJA">Sydney</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam" title="Guam" id="mwCJE">Guam</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu" title="Honolulu" id="mwCJI">Honolulu</a>.<sup about="#mwt995" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-tour-itinerary_226-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;tour-itinerary&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-tour-itinerary-226&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-tour-itinerary-226" id="mwCJM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCJQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCJU">[</span>224<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCJY">]</span></span></a></sup> Crowds in the tens or hundreds of thousands gathered to greet the astronauts in each city.</p>

<p id="mwCJc">In London the astronauts went to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckingham_Palace" title="Buckingham Palace" id="mwCJg">Buckingham Palace</a>, where they were greeted by Queen <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II" title="Elizabeth II" id="mwCJk">Elizabeth II</a>. When they went to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Berlin" title="West Berlin" id="mwCJo">West Berlin</a>, they were given a tour of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall" title="Berlin Wall" id="mwCJs">Berlin Wall</a> by the city's mayor. In Belgrade they were greeted by a crowd of between 400,000 and 500,000 people from the airport to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, where they placed a wreath and were welcomed to a luncheon by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josip_Broz_Tito" title="Josip Broz Tito" id="mwCJw">Josip Broz Tito</a>. In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinshasa" title="Kinshasa" id="mwCJ0">Kinshasa</a>, Democratic Republic of the Congo, they received the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Order_of_the_Leopard" title="National Order of the Leopard" id="mwCJ4">National Order of the Leopard</a> by President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobutu_Sese_Seko" title="Mobutu Sese Seko" id="mwCJ8">Mobutu Sese Seko</a>.<sup about="#mwt998" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-228" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-228&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-228" id="mwCKA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKI">[</span>226<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="27" id="mwCKQ" aria-labelledby="Legacy"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Legacy">Legacy</h2></div>

<section data-mw-section-id="28" id="mwCKU" aria-labelledby="Cultural_significance"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Cultural_significance">Cultural significance</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt999" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCKY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Apollo 11 in popular culture&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1000" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt999" id="mwCKc">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_in_popular_culture" title="Apollo 11 in popular culture">Apollo 11 in popular culture</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCKg"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Land_on_the_Moon_7_21_1969-repair.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCKk"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Land_on_the_Moon_7_21_1969-repair.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Land_on_the_Moon_7_21_1969-repair.jpg/250px-Land_on_the_Moon_7_21_1969-repair.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Land_on_the_Moon_7_21_1969-repair.jpg/500px-Land_on_the_Moon_7_21_1969-repair.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2356" data-file-height="2795" data-file-type="bitmap" height="297" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCKo"></a><figcaption id="mwCKs">A girl holding <i id="mwCKw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post" title="The Washington Post" id="mwCK0">The Washington Post</a></i> newspaper stating <span style="padding-right:.15em;" about="#mwt1001" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCK4" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Double+single&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Double+single&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">"</span><span about="#mwt1001">'</span>The Eagle Has Landed' – Two Men Walk on the Moon"</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwCK8">Humans walking on the Moon and returning safely to Earth accomplished Kennedy's goal set eight years earlier. In Mission Control during the Apollo 11 landing, Kennedy's speech flashed on the screen, followed by the words "TASK ACCOMPLISHED, July 1969".<sup about="#mwt1008" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Launius_229-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Launius&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Launius-229" id="mwCLA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLI">[</span>227<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLM">]</span></span></a></sup> The success of Apollo 11 demonstrated the United States' technological superiority;<sup about="#mwt1011" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Launius_229-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Launius&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Launius-229&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Launius-229" id="mwCLQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLY">[</span>227<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLc">]</span></span></a></sup> and with the success of Apollo 11, America had won the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race" title="Space Race" id="mwCLg">Space Race</a>.<sup about="#mwt1002" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757_230-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin200757&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757-230&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2007&quot;},&quot;page&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;57&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757-230" id="mwCLk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLs">[</span>228<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1005" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESchefter1999288_231-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESchefter1999288&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESchefter1999288-231&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Schefter&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1999&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;288&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchefter1999288-231" id="mwCL0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCL4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCL8">[</span>229<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCME">New phrases permeated into the English language. "If they can send a man to the Moon, why can't they<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCMI">&nbsp;</span>...?" became a common saying following Apollo 11.<sup about="#mwt1017" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-232" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-232&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-232" id="mwCMM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCMQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMU">[</span>230<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMY">]</span></span></a></sup> Armstrong's words on the lunar surface also spun off various parodies.<sup about="#mwt1012" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757_230-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin200757&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757-230&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2007&quot;},&quot;page&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;57&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757-230" id="mwCMc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCMg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMk">[</span>228<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCMs">While most people celebrated the accomplishment, disenfranchised Americans saw it as a symbol of the divide in America, evidenced by protesters led by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Abernathy" title="Ralph Abernathy" id="mwCMw">Ralph Abernathy</a> outside of Kennedy Space Center the day before Apollo 11 launched.<sup about="#mwt1018" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESchefter1999283_233-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESchefter1999283&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESchefter1999283-233&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Schefter&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1999&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;283&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchefter1999283-233" id="mwCM0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCM4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCM8">[</span>231<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNA">]</span></span></a></sup> NASA Administrator <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_O._Paine" title="Thomas O. Paine" id="mwCNE">Thomas Paine</a> met with Abernathy at the occasion, both hoping that the space program can spur progress also in other regards, such as poverty in the US. Paine was then asked, and agreed, to host protesters as spectators at the launch, and Abernathy, awestruck by the spectacle,<sup about="#mwt1021" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979338_106-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979338&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979338-106&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Brooks&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grimwood&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Swenson&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;338&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrooksGrimwoodSwenson1979338-106" id="mwCNI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNQ">[</span>105<span class="cite-bracket" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="History.com is not generally reliable per WP:RSPHISTORY. (November 2025)">better<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>source<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_poetry" title="Jazz poetry" id="mwCNw">Jazz poet</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gil_Scott-Heron" title="Gil Scott-Heron" id="mwCN0">Gil Scott-Heron</a> wrote a poem called "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitey_on_the_Moon" title="Whitey on the Moon" id="mwCN4">Whitey on the Moon</a>" (1970) expressing his view that the mission was emblematic of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_inequality_in_the_United_States" title="Racial inequality in the United States" id="mwCN8">racial inequality in the United States</a>.<sup about="#mwt1025" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757_230-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin200757&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757-230&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2007&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;57&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200757-230" id="mwCOA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCOE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOI">[</span>228<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOM">]</span></span></a></sup> The poem starts with:</p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt1031" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwCOQ" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Poemquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Poemquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;A rat done bit my sister Nell.\n(with Whitey on the moon)\nHer face and arms began to swell.\n(and Whitey's on the moon)\nI can't pay no doctor bill.\n(but Whitey's on the moon)\nTen years from now I'll be paying still.\n(while Whitey's on the moon)\n[...]&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt1031" id="mwCOU"><div class="poem" typeof="mw:Extension/poem" about="#mwt1033" id="mwCOY" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;poem&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;A rat done bit my sister Nell.\n(with Whitey on the moon)\nHer face and arms began to swell.\n(and Whitey's on the moon)\nI can't pay no doctor bill.\n(but Whitey's on the moon)\nTen years from now I'll be paying still.\n(while Whitey's on the moon)\n[...]&quot;}}"><p id="mwCOc">A rat done bit my sister Nell.<br id="mwCOg">
(with Whitey on the moon)<br id="mwCOk">
Her face and arms began to swell.<br id="mwCOo">
(and Whitey's on the moon)<br id="mwCOs">

(while Whitey's on the moon)<br id="mwCO8">
[...]</p></div></blockquote>

<p id="mwCPA">Twenty percent of the world's population watched humans walk on the Moon for the first time.<sup about="#mwt1039" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-235" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-235&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-235" id="mwCPE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCPI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPM">[</span>233<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPQ">]</span></span></a></sup> While Apollo 11 sparked the interest of the world, the follow-on Apollo missions did not hold the interest of the nation.<sup about="#mwt1040" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Launius_229-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Launius&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Launius-229" id="mwCPU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCPY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPc">[</span>227<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPg">]</span></span></a></sup> One possible explanation was the shift in complexity. Landing someone on the Moon was an easy goal to understand; lunar geology was too abstract for the average person. Another is that Kennedy's goal of landing humans on the Moon had already been accomplished.<sup about="#mwt1034" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin200758_236-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin200758&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200758-236&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2007&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;58&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin200758-236" id="mwCPk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCPo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPs">[</span>234<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPw">]</span></span></a></sup> A well-defined objective helped Project Apollo accomplish its goal, but after it was completed it was hard to justify continuing the lunar missions.<sup about="#mwt1043" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-237" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-237&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-237" id="mwCP0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCP4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCP8">[</span>235<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1046" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-238" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-238&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-238" id="mwCQE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCQI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQM">[</span>236<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCQU">While most Americans were proud of their nation's achievements in space exploration, only once during the late 1960s did the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup_Poll" title="Gallup Poll" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCQY">Gallup Poll</a> indicate that a majority of Americans favored "doing more" in space as opposed to "doing less". By 1973, 59 percent of those polled favored cutting spending on space exploration. The Space Race had been won, and Cold War tensions were easing as the US and Soviet Union entered the era of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Détente" title="Détente" id="mwCQc">détente</a>. This was also a time when inflation was rising, which put pressure on the government to reduce spending. The space program was saved due to the perception that it was one of the few government programs that had achieved something great. Drastic cuts, warned <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspar_Weinberger" title="Caspar Weinberger" id="mwCQg">Caspar Weinberger</a>, the deputy director of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Management_and_Budget" title="Office of Management and Budget" id="mwCQk">Office of Management and Budget</a>, might send a signal that "our best years are behind us".<sup about="#mwt1047" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMcCurdy1997106–107_239-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMcCurdy1997106–107&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCurdy1997106–107-239&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;McCurdy&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1997&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;106–107&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCurdy1997106–107-239" id="mwCQo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCQs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQw">[</span>237<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQ0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCQ4">After the Apollo 11 mission, officials from the Soviet Union said landing humans on the Moon was dangerous and unnecessary. At the time the Soviet Union was attempting to retrieve lunar samples robotically. The Soviets publicly denied there was a race to the Moon, and indicated they were not making an attempt.<sup about="#mwt1050" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994631_240-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChaikin1994631&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994631-240&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chaikin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;631&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaikin1994631-240" id="mwCQ8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCRA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRE">[</span>238<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRI">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mstislav_Keldysh" title="Mstislav Keldysh" id="mwCRM">Mstislav Keldysh</a> said in July 1969, "We are concentrating wholly on the creation of large satellite systems." It was revealed in 1989 that the Soviets had tried to send people to the Moon, but were unable due to technological difficulties.<sup about="#mwt1055" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-241" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-241&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-241" id="mwCRQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCRU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRY">[</span>239<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRc">]</span></span></a></sup> The public's reaction in the Soviet Union was mixed. The Soviet government limited the release of information about the lunar landing, which affected the reaction. A portion of the populace did not give it any attention, and another portion was angered by it.<sup about="#mwt1058" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-242" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-242&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-242" id="mwCRg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCRk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRo">[</span>240<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="29" id="mwCRw" aria-labelledby="Spacecraft"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Spacecraft">Spacecraft</h3></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCR0"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Kommandomodul_&quot;Columbia&quot;.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCR4"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Kommandomodul_&quot;Columbia&quot;.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Apollo_11_Kommandomodul_%22Columbia%22.jpg/250px-Apollo_11_Kommandomodul_%22Columbia%22.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Apollo_11_Kommandomodul_%22Columbia%22.jpg/500px-Apollo_11_Kommandomodul_%22Columbia%22.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="2000" data-file-type="bitmap" height="167" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCR8"></a><figcaption id="mwCSA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_Module_Columbia" title="Command Module Columbia" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCSE"><i id="mwCSI">Columbia</i></a> on display in the Milestones of Flight exhibition hall at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum" id="mwCSM">National Air and Space Museum</a></figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwCSQ">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_Module_Columbia" title="Command Module Columbia" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCSU">command module <i id="mwCSY">Columbia</i></a> went on a tour of the United States, visiting 49 state capitals, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C." id="mwCSc">District of Columbia</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchorage,_Alaska" title="Anchorage, Alaska" id="mwCSg">Anchorage, Alaska</a>.<sup about="#mwt1061" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-243" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-243&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-243" id="mwCSk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCSo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCSs">[</span>241<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCSw">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1971, it was transferred to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Institution" title="Smithsonian Institution" id="mwCS0">Smithsonian Institution</a>, and was displayed at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum" id="mwCS4">National Air and Space Museum</a> (NASM) in Washington, DC.<sup about="#mwt1062" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-SIColumbia_244-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;SIColumbia&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-SIColumbia-244" id="mwCS8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCTA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTE">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTI">]</span></span></a></sup> It was in the central <i id="mwCTM">Milestones of Flight</i> exhibition hall in front of the Jefferson Drive entrance, sharing the main hall with other pioneering flight vehicles such as the <i id="mwCTQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Flyer" title="Wright Flyer" id="mwCTU">Wright Flyer</a></i>, <i id="mwCTY"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_of_St._Louis" title="Spirit of St. Louis" id="mwCTc">Spirit of St. Louis</a></i>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_X-1" title="Bell X-1" id="mwCTg">Bell X-1</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_X-15" title="North American X-15" id="mwCTk">North American X-15</a> and <i id="mwCTo"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendship_7" title="Friendship 7" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCTs">Friendship 7</a></i>.<sup about="#mwt1065" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-245" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-245&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-245" id="mwCTw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCT0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCT4">[</span>243<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCT8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCUA"><i id="mwCUE">Columbia</i> was moved in 2017 to the NASM Mary Baker Engen Restoration Hangar at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_F._Udvar-Hazy_Center" title="Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center" id="mwCUI">Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center</a> in Chantilly, Virginia, to be readied for a four-city tour titled <i id="mwCUM">Destination Moon: The Apollo 11 Mission</i>. This included <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Center_Houston" title="Space Center Houston" id="mwCUQ">Space Center Houston</a> from October 14, 2017, to March 18, 2018, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Louis_Science_Center" title="Saint Louis Science Center" id="mwCUU">Saint Louis Science Center</a> from April 14 to September 3, 2018, the Senator John <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz_History_Center" title="Heinz History Center" id="mwCUY">Heinz History Center</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh" title="Pittsburgh" id="mwCUc">Pittsburgh</a> from September 29, 2018, to February 18, 2019, and its last location at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Flight" title="Museum of Flight" id="mwCUg">Museum of Flight</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle" title="Seattle" id="mwCUk">Seattle</a> from March 16 to September 2, 2019.<sup about="#mwt1068" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-SIColumbia_244-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;SIColumbia&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-SIColumbia-244&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-SIColumbia-244" id="mwCUo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCUs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCUw">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCU0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1071" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-246" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-246&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-246" id="mwCU4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCU8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVA">[</span>244<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVE">]</span></span></a></sup> Continued renovations at the Smithsonian allowed time for an additional stop for the capsule, and it was moved to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Museum_Center" title="Cincinnati Museum Center" id="mwCVI">Cincinnati Museum Center</a>. The ribbon cutting ceremony was on September 29, 2019.<sup about="#mwt1074" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-247" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-247&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-247" id="mwCVM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCVQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVU">[</span>245<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCVc">For 40 years Armstrong's and Aldrin's space suits were displayed in the museum's <i id="mwCVg">Apollo to the Moon</i> exhibit,<sup about="#mwt1077" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-248" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-248&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-248" id="mwCVk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCVo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVs">[</span>246<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVw">]</span></span></a></sup> until it permanently closed on December 3, 2018, to be replaced by a new gallery which was scheduled to open in 2022. A special display of Armstrong's suit was unveiled for the 50th anniversary of Apollo 11 in July 2019.<sup about="#mwt1080" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-249" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-249&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-249" id="mwCV0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCV4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCV8">[</span>247<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1083" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-250" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-250&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-250" id="mwCWE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCWI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWM">[</span>248<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The quarantine trailer, the flotation collar and the flotation bags are in the Smithsonian's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_F._Udvar-Hazy_Center" title="Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center" id="mwCWU">Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center</a> annex near <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Dulles_International_Airport" title="Washington Dulles International Airport" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCWY">Washington Dulles International Airport</a> in Chantilly, Virginia, where they are on display along with a test lunar module.<sup about="#mwt1086" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-251" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-251&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-251" id="mwCWc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCWg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWk">[</span>249<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWo">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1089" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-252" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-252&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-252" id="mwCWs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCWw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCW0">[</span>250<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCW4">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1092" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-253" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-253&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-253" id="mwCW8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCXA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCXE">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCXI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCXM"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ArmstrongSuit.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCXQ"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ArmstrongSuit.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/ArmstrongSuit.jpg/250px-ArmstrongSuit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/ArmstrongSuit.jpg/500px-ArmstrongSuit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3024" data-file-height="4032" data-file-type="bitmap" height="333" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCXU"></a><figcaption id="mwCXY">Armstrong's space suit on display at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum" id="mwCXc">National Air and Space Museum</a> in its new exhibit</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwCXg">The descent stage of the LM <i id="mwCXk">Eagle</i> remains on the Moon. In 2009, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Reconnaissance_Orbiter" title="Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter" id="mwCXo">Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter</a> (LRO) imaged the various Apollo landing sites on the surface of the Moon, for the first time with sufficient resolution to see the descent stages of the lunar modules, scientific instruments, and foot trails made by the astronauts.<sup about="#mwt1095" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-254" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-254&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-254" id="mwCXs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCXw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCX0">[</span>252<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCX4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCX8">The remains of the ascent stage are assumed to lie at an unknown location on the lunar surface. The ascent stage, <i id="mwCYA">Eagle</i>, was not tracked after it was jettisoned.  The lunar gravity field is sufficiently non-uniform to make low Moon orbits unstable after a short time, leading the orbiting object to impact the surface.<sup about="#mwt1098" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-255" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-255&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-255" id="mwCYE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCYI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCYM">[</span>253<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCYQ">]</span></span></a></sup> However, using a program developed by NASA, and high-resolution lunar gravity data, a paper was published, in 2021, indicating that <i id="mwCYU">Eagle</i> might still be in orbit as late as 2020. Using the orbital elements published by NASA, a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_method" title="Monte Carlo method" id="mwCYY">Monte Carlo method</a> was used to generate parameter sets that bracket the uncertainties in these elements. All simulations, of the orbit, predicted that <i id="mwCYc">Eagle</i> would never impact the lunar surface.<sup about="#mwt1101" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Impact_256-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Impact&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Impact-256&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Impact-256" id="mwCYg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCYk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCYo">[</span>254<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCYs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1102" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCYw" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;multiple
