Center">Cincinnati Museum Center</a> in 2019</div></div></div></div><span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1102"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Pages_using_multiple_image_with_auto_scaled_images"></span>

<p id="mwCY0">In March 2012 a team of specialists financed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon.com" title="Amazon.com" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCY4">Amazon</a> founder <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos" title="Jeff Bezos" id="mwCY8">Jeff Bezos</a> located the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocketdyne_F-1" title="Rocketdyne F-1" id="mwCZA">F-1 engines</a> from the S-IC stage that launched Apollo 11 into space. They were found on the Atlantic seabed using advanced sonar scanning.<sup about="#mwt1106" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-257" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-257&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-257" id="mwCZE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCZI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZM">[</span>255<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZQ">]</span></span></a></sup> His team brought parts of two of the five engines to the surface. In July 2013, a conservator discovered a serial number under the rust on one of the engines raised from the Atlantic, which NASA confirmed was from Apollo 11.<sup about="#mwt1109" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-258" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-258&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-258" id="mwCZU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCZY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZc">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1112" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-259" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-259&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-259" id="mwCZk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCZo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZs">[</span>257<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZw">]</span></span></a></sup> The S-IVB third stage which performed Apollo 11's trans-lunar injection remains in a solar orbit near to that of Earth.<sup about="#mwt1115" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-260" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-260&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-260" id="mwCZ0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCZ4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCZ8">[</span>258<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCaA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCaE"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:430-L1-S1_640.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCaI"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:430-L1-S1_640.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/430-L1-S1_640.jpg/250px-430-L1-S1_640.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/430-L1-S1_640.jpg/500px-430-L1-S1_640.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2746" data-file-height="1510" data-file-type="bitmap" height="137" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCaM"></a><figcaption id="mwCaQ">Pieces of fabric and wood from the first airplane, the 1903 <i id="mwCaU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Flyer" title="Wright Flyer" id="mwCaY">Wright Flyer</a></i>, traveled to the Moon in Apollo 11's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Module_Eagle" title="Lunar Module Eagle" id="mwCac">Lunar Module <i id="mwCag">Eagle</i></a> and are displayed at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Brothers_National_Memorial" title="Wright Brothers National Memorial" id="mwCak">Wright Brothers National Memorial</a>.</figcaption></figure>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="30" id="mwCao" aria-labelledby="Moon_rocks"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Moon_rocks">Moon rocks</h3></div>

<p id="mwCas">The main repository for the Apollo Moon rocks is the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Sample_Laboratory_Facility" title="Lunar Sample Laboratory Facility" id="mwCaw">Lunar Sample Laboratory Facility</a> at the Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston" title="Houston" id="mwCa0">Houston</a>, Texas. For safekeeping, there is also a smaller collection stored at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sands_Test_Facility" title="White Sands Test Facility" id="mwCa4">White Sands Test Facility</a> near <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Cruces,_New_Mexico" title="Las Cruces, New Mexico" id="mwCa8">Las Cruces, New Mexico</a>. Most of the rocks are stored in nitrogen to keep them free of moisture. They are handled only indirectly, using special tools. Over 100 research laboratories worldwide conduct studies of the samples; approximately 500 samples are prepared and sent to investigators every year.<sup about="#mwt1118" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-261" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-261&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-261" id="mwCbA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCbE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCbI">[</span>259<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCbM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1121" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-262" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-262&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-262" id="mwCbQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCbU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCbY">[</span>260<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCbc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCbg">In November 1969, Nixon asked NASA to make up about 250 presentation <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_lunar_sample_display" title="Apollo 11 lunar sample display" id="mwCbk">Apollo 11 lunar sample displays</a> for 135 nations, the fifty states of the United States and its possessions, and the United Nations. Each display included Moon dust from Apollo 11 and flags, including one of the Soviet Union, taken along by Apollo 11. The rice-sized particles were four small pieces of Moon soil weighing about 50<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCbo">&nbsp;</span>mg and were enveloped in a clear acrylic button about as big as a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_dollar_(United_States_coin)" title="Half dollar (United States coin)" id="mwCbs">United States half-dollar coin</a>. This acrylic button magnified the grains of lunar dust. Nixon gave the Apollo 11 lunar sample displays as goodwill gifts in 1970.<sup about="#mwt1124" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-263" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-263&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-263" id="mwCbw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCb0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCb4">[</span>261<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCb8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1125" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-264" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-264&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-264" id="mwCcA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCcE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcI">[</span>262<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="31" id="mwCcQ" aria-labelledby="Experiment_results"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Experiment_results">Experiment results</h3></div>

<p id="mwCcU">The Passive Seismic Experiment ran until the command uplink failed on August 25, 1969. The downlink failed on December 14, 1969.<sup about="#mwt1126" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBatesLauderdaleKernaghan19792-3_&amp;_4-32_265-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBatesLauderdaleKernaghan19792-3 &amp; 4-32&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBatesLauderdaleKernaghan19792-3_&amp;_4-32-265&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Bates&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lauderdale&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Kernaghan&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1979&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2-3 &amp; 4-32&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBatesLauderdaleKernaghan19792-3_&amp;_4-32-265" id="mwCcY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCcc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcg">[</span>263<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCck">]</span></span></a></sup><!-- Hyphens, not ndashes --> <span about="#mwt1129" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCco" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;As of&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:As_of&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2025&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">As of 2025</span><sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;" about="#mwt1129"><a rel="mw:ExtLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Apollo_11&amp;action=edit" class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Apollo_11&amp;action=edit"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span>update<span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></a></sup><span typeof="mw:Nowiki" about="#mwt1129"></span><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements_from_2025" about="#mwt1129"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements" about="#mwt1129" id="mwCcs">, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_Ranging_Retroflector" title="Laser Ranging Retroflector" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCcw">Lunar Laser Ranging experiment</a> remains operational.<sup about="#mwt1132" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-266" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-266&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-266" id="mwCc0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCc4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCc8">[</span>264<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="32" id="mwCdE" aria-labelledby="Moonwalk_camera"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Moonwalk_camera">Moonwalk camera</h3></div>

<p id="mwCdI">The Hasselblad camera used during the moonwalk was thought to be lost or left on the Moon's surface.<sup about="#mwt1135" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-267" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-267&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-267" id="mwCdM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCdQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdU">[</span>265<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="33" id="mwCdc" aria-labelledby="Lunar_Module_Eagle_memorabilia"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Lunar_Module_Eagle_memorabilia">Lunar Module <i id="mwCdg">Eagle</i> memorabilia</h3></div>

<p id="mwCdk">In 2015, after Armstrong died in 2012, his widow contacted the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum" id="mwCdo">National Air and Space Museum</a> to inform them she had found a white cloth bag in one of Armstrong's closets. The bag contained various items, which should have been left behind in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunar_Module_Eagle" title="Lunar Module Eagle" id="mwCds">Lunar Module <i id="mwCdw">Eagle</i></a>, including the 16mm Data Acquisition Camera that had been used to capture images of the first Moon landing.<sup about="#mwt1138" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-268" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-268&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-268" id="mwCd0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCd4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCd8">[</span>266<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCeA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1141" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-269" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-269&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-269" id="mwCeE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCeI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCeM">[</span>267<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCeQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The camera is currently on display at the National Air and Space Museum.<sup about="#mwt1144" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-270" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-270&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-270" id="mwCeU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCeY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCec">[</span>268<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCeg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="34" id="mwCek" aria-labelledby="Anniversary_events"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Anniversary_events">Anniversary events</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1145" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCeo" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;further&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Further&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Apollo 11 anniversaries&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1146" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1145" id="mwCes">Further information: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_anniversaries" title="Apollo 11 anniversaries">Apollo 11 anniversaries</a></div>

<section data-mw-section-id="35" id="mwCew" aria-labelledby="40th_anniversary"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="40th_anniversary"><span id="40th_anniversary_events"></span>40th anniversary</h4></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCe0"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Command_Module_in_Hangar.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCe4"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_Command_Module_in_Hangar.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Apollo_11_Command_Module_in_Hangar.jpg/250px-Apollo_11_Command_Module_in_Hangar.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Apollo_11_Command_Module_in_Hangar.jpg/500px-Apollo_11_Command_Module_in_Hangar.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="5259" data-file-height="3544" data-file-type="bitmap" height="168" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCe8"></a><figcaption id="mwCfA"><i id="mwCfE">Columbia</i> at the Mary Baker Engen Restoration Hangar</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwCfI">On July 15, 2009, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_(magazine)" title="Life (magazine)" id="mwCfM">Life.com</a> released a photo gallery of previously unpublished photos of the astronauts taken by <i id="mwCfQ">Life</i> photographer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Morse" title="Ralph Morse" id="mwCfU">Ralph Morse</a> prior to the Apollo 11 launch.<sup about="#mwt1149" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-271" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-271&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-271" id="mwCfY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCfc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfg">[</span>269<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfk">]</span></span></a></sup> From July 16 to 24, 2009, NASA streamed the original mission audio on its website in real time 40 years to the minute after the events occurred.<sup about="#mwt1152" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-272" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-272&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-272" id="mwCfo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCfs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfw">[</span>270<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCf0">]</span></span></a></sup> It is in the process of restoring the video footage and has released a preview of key moments.<sup about="#mwt1155" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-273" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-273&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-273" id="mwCf4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCf8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgA">[</span>271<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgE">]</span></span></a></sup> In July 2010, air-to-ground voice recordings and film footage shot in Mission Control during the Apollo 11 powered descent and landing was re-synchronized and released for the first time.<sup about="#mwt1158" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-274" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-274&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-274" id="mwCgI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCgM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgQ">[</span>272<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgU">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Presidential_Library_and_Museum" title="John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum" id="mwCgY">John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum</a> set up an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Flash" title="Adobe Flash" id="mwCgc">Adobe Flash</a> website that rebroadcasts the transmissions of Apollo 11 from launch to landing on the Moon.<sup about="#mwt1161" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-275" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-275&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-275" id="mwCgg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCgk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgo">[</span>273<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCgw">On July 20, 2009, Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins met with President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama" title="Barack Obama" id="mwCg0">Barack Obama</a> at the White House.<sup about="#mwt1164" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-276" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-276&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-276" id="mwCg4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCg8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChA">[</span>274<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChE">]</span></span></a></sup> "We expect that there is, as we speak, another generation of kids out there who are looking up at the sky and are going to be the next Armstrong, Collins, and Aldrin", Obama said. "We want to make sure that NASA is going to be there for them when they want to take their journey."<sup about="#mwt1167" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-277" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-277&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-277" id="mwChI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwChM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChQ">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChU">]</span></span></a></sup> On August 7, 2009, an act of Congress awarded the three astronauts a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Gold_Medal" title="Congressional Gold Medal" id="mwChY">Congressional Gold Medal</a>, the highest civilian award in the United States. The bill was sponsored by Florida Senator <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson_(politician)" title="Bill Nelson (politician)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwChc">Bill Nelson</a> and Florida Representative <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Grayson" title="Alan Grayson" id="mwChg">Alan Grayson</a>.<sup about="#mwt1170" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-278" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-278&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-278" id="mwChk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCho"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChs">[</span>276<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1173" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-279" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-279&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-279" id="mwCh0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCh4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCh8">[</span>277<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCiA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCiE">A group of British scientists interviewed as part of the anniversary events reflected on the significance of the Moon landing:</p>

<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1244412712" about="#mwt1174" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles mw:Transclusion" id="mwCiI" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Template:Blockquote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;blockquote&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Blockquote&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;It was carried out in a technically brilliant way with risks taken&amp;nbsp;... that would be inconceivable in the risk-averse world of today&amp;nbsp;... The Apollo programme is arguably the greatest technical achievement of mankind to date&amp;nbsp;... nothing since Apollo has come close [to] the excitement that was generated by those astronauts—Armstrong, Aldrin and the 10 others who followed them.&lt;ref&gt;{{Cite news |title=Moon landings: British scientists salute space heroes |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/space/5848707/Moon-landings-British-scientists-salute-space-heroes.html |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |location=London |date=July 17, 2009 |access-date=June 14, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130308224145/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/space/5848707/Moon-landings-British-scientists-salute-space-heroes.html |archive-date=March 8, 2013 |df=mdy}}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><blockquote class="templatequote " about="#mwt1174" id="mwCiM"><p>It was carried out in a technically brilliant way with risks taken<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>... that would be inconceivable in the risk-averse world of today<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>... The Apollo programme is arguably the greatest technical achievement of mankind to date<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>... nothing since Apollo has come close [to] the excitement that was generated by those astronauts—Armstrong, Aldrin and the 10 others who followed them.<sup about="#mwt1178" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-280" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-280&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-280" id="mwCiQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCiU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCiY">[</span>278<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCic">]</span></span></a></sup></p></blockquote>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="36" id="mwCig" aria-labelledby="50th_anniversary"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="50th_anniversary">50th anniversary</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1181" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCik" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;further&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Further&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Apollo 11 50th Anniversary commemorative coins&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1182" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1181" id="mwCio">Further information: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_50th_Anniversary_commemorative_coins" title="Apollo 11 50th Anniversary commemorative coins">Apollo 11 50th Anniversary commemorative coins</a></div>

<p id="mwCis">In June 2015, Congressman <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Posey" title="Bill Posey" id="mwCiw">Bill Posey</a> introduced resolution H.R. 2726 to the 114th session of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives" title="United States House of Representatives" id="mwCi0">United States House of Representatives</a> directing the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Mint" title="United States Mint" id="mwCi4">United States Mint</a> to design and sell commemorative coins in gold, silver and clad for the 50th anniversary of the Apollo 11 mission. On January 24, 2019, the Mint released the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_Fiftieth_Anniversary_commemorative_coins" title="Apollo 11 Fiftieth Anniversary commemorative coins" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCi8">Apollo 11 Fiftieth Anniversary commemorative coins</a> to the public on its website.<sup about="#mwt1184" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-281" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-281&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-281" id="mwCjA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCjE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjI">[</span>279<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1187" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-282" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-282&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-282" id="mwCjQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCjU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjY">[</span>280<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCjg">A documentary film, <i id="mwCjk"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_(2019_film)" title="Apollo 11 (2019 film)" id="mwCjo">Apollo 11</a></i>, with restored footage of the 1969 event, premiered in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX" title="IMAX" id="mwCjs">IMAX</a> on March 1, 2019, and broadly in theaters on March 8.<sup about="#mwt1190" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-283" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-283&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-283" id="mwCjw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCj0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCj4">[</span>281<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCj8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1193" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-284" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-284&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-284" id="mwCkA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCkE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkI">[</span>282<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCkQ">The Smithsonian Institute's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Air_and_Space_Museum" title="National Air and Space Museum" id="mwCkU">National Air and Space Museum</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA" title="NASA" id="mwCkY">NASA</a> sponsored the "Apollo 50 Festival" on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Mall" title="National Mall" id="mwCkc">National Mall</a> in Washington DC. The three-day (July 18 to 20, 2019) outdoor festival featured hands-on exhibits and activities, live performances, and speakers such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Savage" title="Adam Savage" id="mwCkg">Adam Savage</a> and NASA scientists.<sup about="#mwt1196" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-285" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-285&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-285" id="mwCkk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCko"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCks">[</span>283<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCk0"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_projected_on_the_washington_monument.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCk4"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apollo_11_projected_on_the_washington_monument.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Apollo_11_projected_on_the_washington_monument.jpg/250px-Apollo_11_projected_on_the_washington_monument.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Apollo_11_projected_on_the_washington_monument.jpg/500px-Apollo_11_projected_on_the_washington_monument.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3532" data-file-height="5298" data-file-type="bitmap" height="285" width="190" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 0.75" id="mwCk8"></a><figcaption id="mwClA">A Saturn V rocket projected onto the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Monument" title="Washington Monument" id="mwClE">Washington Monument</a> during the Apollo 11 50th anniversary show</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwClI">As part of the festival, a projection of the <span about="#mwt1197" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwClM" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;363&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;adj&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;on&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">363-foot (111</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt1197">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt1197">m)</span> tall <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_V" title="Saturn V" id="mwClQ">Saturn V</a> rocket was displayed on the east face of the <span about="#mwt1198" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwClU" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;555&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;adj&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;on&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">555-foot (169</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt1198">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt1198">m)</span> tall <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Monument" title="Washington Monument" id="mwClY">Washington Monument</a> from July 16 to the 20th from 9:30<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwClc">&nbsp;</span>pm until 11:30<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwClg">&nbsp;</span>pm (EDT). The program  included a 17-minute show that combined full-motion video projected on the Washington Monument to recreate the assembly and launch of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_V" title="Saturn V" id="mwClk">Saturn V</a> rocket.<sup about="#mwt1201" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Apollo_50_Go_For_the_Moon_286-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Apollo 50 Go For the Moon&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Apollo_50_Go_For_the_Moon-286&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Apollo_50_Go_For_the_Moon-286" id="mwClo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCls"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwClw">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCl0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCl4">The projection was joined by a <span about="#mwt1202" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCl8" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;convert&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Convert&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;40&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;ft&quot;},&quot;adj&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;on&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">40-foot (12</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt1202">&nbsp;</span><span about="#mwt1202">m)</span> wide recreation of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center" title="Kennedy Space Center" id="mwCmA">Kennedy Space Center</a> countdown clock and two large video screens showing archival footage to recreate the time leading up to the moon landing. There were three shows per night on July 19–20, with the last show on Saturday, delayed slightly so the portion where Armstrong first set foot on the Moon would happen exactly 50 years to the second after the actual event.<sup about="#mwt1203" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Apollo_50_Go_For_the_Moon_286-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Apollo 50 Go For the Moon&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Apollo_50_Go_For_the_Moon-286" id="mwCmE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCmI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmM">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCmU">On July 19, 2019, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Doodle" title="Google Doodle" id="mwCmY">Google Doodle</a> paid tribute to the Apollo 11 Moon landing, complete with a link to an animated YouTube video with voiceover by astronaut <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Collins_(astronaut)" title="Michael Collins (astronaut)" id="mwCmc">Michael Collins</a>.<sup about="#mwt1206" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-287" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-287&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-287" id="mwCmg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCmk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmo">[</span>285<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCms">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1209" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-288" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-288&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-288" id="mwCmw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCm0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCm4">[</span>286<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCm8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCnA">Aldrin, Collins, and Armstrong's sons were hosted by President <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump" id="mwCnE">Donald Trump</a> in the Oval Office.<sup about="#mwt1212" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-289" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-289&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-289" id="mwCnI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCnM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCnQ">[</span>287<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCnU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1215" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-290" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-290&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-290" id="mwCnY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCnc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCng">[</span>288<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCnk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section></section><section data-mw-section-id="37" id="mwCno" aria-labelledby="Films_and_documentaries"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Films_and_documentaries">Films and documentaries</h2></div>

<li id="mwCoM"><i id="mwCoQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonwalk_One" title="Moonwalk One" id="mwCoU">Moonwalk One</a></i>, a 1971 documentary film by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theo_Kamecke" title="Theo Kamecke" id="mwCoY">Theo Kamecke</a><sup about="#mwt1222" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-guardian-20090526_292-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;guardian-20090526&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-guardian-20090526-292&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-20090526-292" id="mwCoc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCog"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCok">[</span>290<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCoo">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCos"><i id="mwCow">Apollo 11: As It Happened</i>, a 1994 six-hour documentary on ABC News' coverage of the event<sup about="#mwt1225" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-floridatoday-19940717_293-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;floridatoday-19940717&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-floridatoday-19940717-293&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-floridatoday-19940717-293" id="mwCo0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCo4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCo8">[</span>291<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCpA">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCpE"><i id="mwCpI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_(1996_film)" title="Apollo 11 (1996 film)" id="mwCpM">Apollo<span class="nowrap" about="#mwt1229" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCpQ" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;nbsp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Nbsp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span></span>11</a></i>, a 1996 docudrama<sup about="#mwt1228" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-294" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-294&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-294" id="mwCpU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCpY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCpc">[</span>292<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCpg">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCpk"><i id="mwCpo"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Man_(film)" title="First Man (film)" id="mwCps">First Man</a></i>, 2018 film by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damien_Chazelle" title="Damien Chazelle" id="mwCpw">Damien Chazelle</a> based on the 2005 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_R._Hansen" title="James R. Hansen" id="mwCp0">James R. Hansen</a> book <i id="mwCp4"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Man:_The_Life_of_Neil_A._Armstrong" title="First Man: The Life of Neil A. Armstrong" id="mwCp8">First Man: The Life of Neil A. Armstrong</a></i></li>
<li id="mwCqA"><i id="mwCqE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11_(2019_film)" title="Apollo 11 (2019 film)" id="mwCqI">Apollo 11</a></i>, a 2019 documentary film by Todd Douglas Miller with restored footage of the 1969 event<sup about="#mwt1233" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-nyt-20190227_295-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;nyt-20190227&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-nyt-20190227-295&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-nyt-20190227-295" id="mwCqM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCqQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqU">[</span>293<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqY">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1236" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-296" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-296&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-296" id="mwCqc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCqg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqk">[</span>294<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqo">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCqs"><i id="mwCqw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chasing_the_Moon_(2019_film)" title="Chasing the Moon (2019 film)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCq0">Chasing the Moon</a></i>, a July 2019 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS" title="PBS" id="mwCq4">PBS</a> three-night six-hour documentary, directed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Stone_(director)" title="Robert Stone (director)" id="mwCq8">Robert Stone</a>, examined the events leading up to the mission. An accompanying book of the same name was also released.<sup about="#mwt1239" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-spacereview-20190708_297-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;spacereview-20190708&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-spacereview-20190708-297&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-spacereview-20190708-297" id="mwCrA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCrE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrI">[</span>295<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrM">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwCrQ"><i id="mwCrU">8 Days: To the Moon and Back</i>, a PBS and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Studios" title="BBC Studios" id="mwCrY">BBC Studios</a> 2019 documentary film by Anthony Philipson re-enacting major portions of the mission using mission audio recordings, new studio footage, NASA and news archives, and computer-generated imagery.<sup about="#mwt1242" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-298" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-298&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-298" id="mwCrc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCrg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrk">[</span>296<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCro">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

<div class="mw-references-wrap" typeof="mw:Extension/references" about="#mwt1248" id="mwCss" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;references&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;,&quot;responsive&quot;:&quot;1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"><ol class="mw-references references" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCsw"><li about="#cite_note-58" id="cite_note-58" data-mw-footnote-number="a"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwCs0"><a href="#cite_ref-58" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwCs4"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwCs8">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-58" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">The role of the backup crew was to train and be prepared to fly in the event something happened to the prime crew.<sup about="#mwt257" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-57" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-57&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-57" id="mwCtA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCtE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCtI">[</span>57<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCtM">]</span></span></a></sup> Backup crews, according to the rotation, were assigned as the prime crew three missions after their assignment of backups.</span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-transcript-147" id="cite_note-transcript-147" data-mw-footnote-number="b"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwCtQ"><a href="#cite_ref-transcript_147-0" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwCtU"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwCtY">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-transcript-147" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">Eric Jones of the <i id="mwCtc">Apollo Lunar Surface Journal</i> explains that the indefinite article "a" was intended, whether or not it was said; the intention was to contrast <i id="mwCtg">a man</i> (an individual's action) and <i id="mwCtk">mankind</i> (as a species).<sup about="#mwt647" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-146" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-146&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-146" id="mwCto"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCts"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCtw">[</span>145<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCt0">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>
</ol></div></div>
